## Scope

A path counts as a code file when its extension is one of: `.java`, `.cc`, `.h`, `.c`, `.cpp`, `.hh`, `.hpp`, `.inc`, `.py`, `.bzl`, `.proto`, `.go`, `.js`, `.ts`, `.sh`, `.star`.

- Tracked paths: 13914
- Code files in the agent queue: 6707
- Other tracked paths (docs, BUILD files without those extensions, archives, images, testdata): 7207. Those are not given a per-file behavior review. Extension totals for them are in the appendix.

## Progress

- Code files reviewed: 6707 / 6707
- Last section appended: `tools/upload_bazel_mirror.sh` (queue index 6707). The queue is complete.

## Language, runtime, and third-party notes

Entries below call out Java, C++, Python, or Starlark semantics that Rust does not share, and third-party libraries Bazel links that zel either reimplemented or does not vendor yet. Per-file sections repeat a note only when that file's behavior depends on it.

- Java `String` is UTF-16 code units. `length`, `charAt`, `substring`, and `Pattern` count and slice on `char` values, so a supplementary character (emoji, many CJK extensions) is two units. Rust `str` methods count Unicode scalar values or bytes. A difference is recorded only when the Bazel file uses those operations on data that can be non-BMP, or when the index is part of a digest, a flag, or an error string.
- Java `HashMap` / `HashSet` iteration order is not insertion order. Zel structures that sort or preserve order will diverge wherever Bazel prints or hashes an unordered collection without an explicit sort.
- Java integer arithmetic wraps silently (`int`/`long`). Rust debug builds panic on overflow; release builds wrap. Call sites that rely on wraparound are called out.
- Bazel error text often comes from the JDK (`java.util.regex`, `java.nio.file`), Guava, Gson, or Apache Commons Compress. A Rust reimplementation that returns a different message is a difference even when the exit code matches.
- Bazel's Linux sandbox is the C++ helper under `src/main/tools/linux-sandbox*.cc`. Zel's `zel-sandbox` builds that command line and, when the helper is absent, falls back to `process-wrapper` without namespaces.

### `combine_distfiles.py`
- Bazel lines: 50
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - No port of `main` (lines 28–46). It writes `os.path.join(os.getcwd(), sys.argv[1])` as a `zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED` archive of `sorted(sys.argv[2:])`. `.tar` inputs go through `src.create_embedded_tools_lib.copy_tar_to_zip` (lines 24, 41–42) and `.zip` inputs through `copy_zip_to_zip` (lines 25, 43–44), both with `_normalize` stripping a leading `./` (lines 37–38). Any other suffix raises `Exception("unknown archive type \"%s\"" % input_file)` (line 46). Searches under `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates` (including `zel-bazel-tools`) for `combine_distfiles`, `copy_tar_to_zip`, `copy_zip_to_zip`, `create_embedded_tools`, and `unknown archive type` found no counterpart.
  - Python `zipfile` deflate and entry ordering are the CPython implementation. Zel has no equivalent writer, so timestamp, compression-level, and extra-field behavior cannot match.

### `combine_distfiles_to_tar.sh`
- Bazel lines: 54
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - The script is absent from zel. It builds one tar of every member of the input archives (lines 19–54).
  - Output path is `${PWD}/$1` (line 25). Inputs are `${PWD}/$i` (line 35). Zel has no equivalent CLI.
  - `*.zip` is unpacked with `unzip -q` and `*.tar` with `tar xf` (lines 36–40). Other suffixes leave `UNPACK` unset and fail under `set -u`. Zel does not shell out to `unzip` or `tar` for this pack step.
  - Temp dir is `mktemp -d ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/bazel.XXXXXXXX` with `trap rm -fr` (lines 28–30). A second `mktemp` holds the file list (`bazel-distfile-files.XXXXXXXX`, lines 50–51).
  - Only regular files are archived: `find . -type f | sort` (line 52). Directories, symlinks, and empty dirs are dropped. Order is byte-wise `sort` of the `find` paths.
  - Ownership is forced to 0. GNU tar gets `--group=0 --owner=0`; Darwin (`uname -s` = Darwin) gets `--gid=0 --uid=0` (lines 43–46). Reproducibility depends on the inputs already having canonical timestamps (comment lines 20–23); this script does not rewrite mtimes.
  - No zel code references `combine_distfiles_to_tar` or `bazel-distfile-files`.

The scratch stage also assembles an `@bazel_tools` install archive and a `libblaze.jar` run with `java -jar`. Zel’s build does not need a JDK. Embedded tools are `include_bytes!` tables from `resources/` and `builtins/` in `crates/zel-bazel-tools/build.rs` lines 1–39.
  - Bazel failures use `fail` (`buildenv.sh` lines 65–72): blank line, `ERROR: …` on stderr, exit status of the failed command or 1. Messages include `Could not build Bazel`, `Could not find freshly built Bazel binary at '…'`, and `Could not copy '…'`. A phase file is dumped on exit. Zel `package_zel.sh` lines 73–75 print `Unknown option: $1` and exit 1. A missing binary is a `cargo`/`cp` error under `set -u`/`pipefail`, not those strings.

Zel adds `.exe` when the detected or `--os` value is `windows`, and accepts `--os`, `--arch`, and `--target`. It does not build JNI.

### `distdir.bzl`
- Bazel lines: 100
- Zel counterpart: none (nearest related code is `crates/zel-bzlmod/src/download.rs`, which only checks a distdir during fetch)
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - Lines 37–99 define the `repo_cache_tar` repository rule (loaded by Bazel’s `extensions.bzl` as `bootstrap_repo_cache` / `bazel_tools_repo_cache`). This file does not implement `--distdir` lookup itself. Zel has no rule or embedded `.bzl` with this name. `download.rs` distdir basename search (around lines 991–1011 and 1378–1397) and cache layout `content_addressable/<algo>/<hex>/file` only consult a distdir while fetching. They do not build this cache tarball.
  - Lines 16 and 45–47 load and call `parse_http_artifacts` / `parse_registry_files` from `//src/tools/bzlmod:utils.bzl`. `repos` selects lockfile `http_archive` / `http_file` / `http_jar` artifacts. `module_files` is forwarded, but `parse_registry_files` ignores it and returns every `registryFileHashes` entry. Zel has neither parser.
  - Lines 49–78 prefetch those artifacts into a repository-cache tree. `"integrity" in artifact` and `"sha256" in artifact` test key presence, so a present key whose value is `None` still enters the branch. A repeated integrity reuses `integrity_to_sha256` and `continue`s (57–59). Otherwise it `ctx.delete("./tempfile")` (61–63, so a `--experimental_repository_cache_hardlinks` hardlink can be replaced) and `ctx.download`s to `./tempfile` with `integrity` to learn `sha256` (64), then downloads again to `content_addressable/sha256/%s/file` (73–74). A repeated sha256 `continue`s (70–71). If neither key is present it `fail`s with `Could not find integrity or sha256 hash for artifact %s` (78). Zel has no equivalent prefetch, dedup, double download, hardlink delete, or that error string.
  - Lines 18–34 and 80–87 always write `README.md` (one bullet per first-seen URL and SHA256, in `http_artifacts + registry_files` order) and a `BUILD` that loads `@rules_pkg//pkg:tar.bzl` `pkg_tar`, with public `filegroup` `files` and public `pkg_tar` `archives` (`strip_prefix = "external/" + ctx.attr.name`, `package_dir = dirname`). Zel’s `pkg_tar` (`crates/zel-bazel-tools/resources/tools/build_defs/pkg/pkg.bzl`) is not driven by a generator like this.
  - Lines 90–99: attrs are `lockfile` (default `Label("//:MODULE.bazel.lock")`), `dirname` (default `"repository_cache"`), `repos` (`string_list`), and `module_files` (`label_list`). The `repository_rule` sets no `local`, `environ`, or `doc`. Zel does not expose this rule or these defaults.
  - This file never indexes or slices strings, so Starlark code-point indexing versus Java UTF-16 does not apply. `integrity_to_sha256` and `seen_sha256` are only keyed, not iterated. README lines and BUILD `srcs` follow the list order of `http_artifacts + registry_files` (line 53), which is the helpers’ JSON-object key order.

### `examples/py/bin.py`
- Bazel lines: 3
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - No `examples/py/bin.py` (or `examples/py/`) in the zel tree. Other `bin.py` hits are vendored `rules_python` tests and examples, not this sample.
  - The program is `print("Fib(5)=%d" % lib.Fib(5))`, a function call with no `from __future__ import print_function`. That is Python 3. Bazel runs it under the toolchain interpreter (default PY3). The launcher stub in `python_bootstrap_template.txt` still carries Py2-compat futures (`print_function`, and a comment that the stub itself targets 2.7). A Rust-hosted `py_binary` does not emit that stub (`py_*` without a toolchain is an analysis error in `zel-rules`). Executing this source as-is is a `SyntaxError` on Python 2.
  - The only string is a plain `"..."` literal. No `u` prefix and no `unicode()`. Python 3 treats it as Unicode text. Python 2 would treat it as a byte string. The file does not force either.
  - The source has no shebang. Bazel `py_binary` writes a separate stub whose first line is `#!/usr/bin/env python3` (`DEFAULT_STUB_SHEBANG` in `rules_python` `py_runtime_info.bzl`) and then runs this file. Copying `bin.py` itself as the executable leaves a file the kernel cannot exec.

### `scripts/bazel-bisect.sh`
- Bazel lines: 101
- Zel counterpart: `none`

  - Zel has no first-party git-bisect helper. The only hit, `third_party/bcr/protobuf/33.4/upb/wire/decode_fast/bisect.sh`, is a vendored upb fasttable numeric bisect, not a Bazel/zel source bisect.
  - Usage: `bazel-bisect.sh GOOD_COMMIT BAD_COMMIT [<bazel arguments>...]`. It clones `https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel` (override `BAZEL_REPO`) into `$HOME/os-bazel-bisect` (override `BAZEL_DIR`), `git fetch --tags`, `git checkout master`, then `git bisect start`, `git bisect good`, `git bisect bad`, `git bisect run /tmp/bisect.sh`, and `git bisect reset`. The outer script exits with the `git bisect run` status.
  - Each step builds with `"$BAZEL_BINARY" build //src:bazel` (`BAZEL_BINARY` defaults to `$(which bazel)`), copies `bazel-bin/src/bazel` to `/tmp/bazel.bisect`, optionally runs `"$TMP_BIN" clean` when `BAZEL_BISECT_WITH_CLEAN=y`, then runs `"$TMP_BIN" $BAZEL_ARGUMENTS` in the original cwd, then `"$TMP_BIN" shutdown`. There is no hardcoded test target and no `--version` flag.
  - Exit convention matches `git bisect run`: the user command’s status is preserved (`0` = good, `1`–`124` and `126`–`127` = bad, `125` = skip, `128`–`255` = abort). A failed `//src:bazel` bootstrap exits `1` (counted bad, not skipped). `clean` and `shutdown` failures are ignored (`|| true`).
  - Hardcoded Bazel names: binary `bazel`, target `//src:bazel`, output `bazel-bin/src/bazel`, temp `/tmp/bazel.bisect`, repo `bazelbuild/bazel`, branch `master`. A zel port would need `zel`, target `//crates:zel` (`rust_binary` in `crates/BUILD.bazel`), and output `bazel-bin/crates/zel`. The script never passes a version flag. It execs the freshly built binary directly, so `USE_BAZEL_VERSION` / `.bazelversion` (and zel’s `USE_ZEL_VERSION`) do not apply inside the loop.

### `scripts/bazel_lockfile_merge_test.sh`
- Bazel lines: 469
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - The test drives `scripts/bazel-lockfile-merge.jq` as a git-merge-style driver (`jq -s` on base, left, right, then overwrite left). Zel has no merge driver under `crates/zel-bzlmod` or `scripts`. `crates/zel-bzlmod/src/lockfile.rs` only reads and writes a version-28 JSON lockfile.
  - Nested maps are a shallow union. Values are uniquified in input order (base first), then last unique value wins, so a side that still equals the base does not clobber the other side. The synthetic case keeps left's `repo1: new_args` over right's `old_args`, takes right's changed `bzlTransitiveDigest` when left omits that extension, and unions yanked versions and per-factor extension entries (`aarch64` and `amd64`).
  - The merger never emits a conflict message and is expected to exit 0 in every case, including version skew. The harness only fails the test on a non-zero `jq`/`sh` status (`merge failed`) or a `diff` mismatch (`output differs`).
  - Only inputs whose `lockFileVersion` equals the maximum are merged. A lower version (the v9 right file) is dropped and the higher-version file is kept byte-for-byte. If the max-version set cannot be merged (the v7/v8/v9 case, which lacks the v10+ maps), the script returns the first file unchanged, still with exit 0.
  - `facts` are merged the same way, but per extension only entries at the highest `factsVersions` value survive (left's version 1 `old_key` is dropped; right's version 2 `new_key` is kept). The output `factsVersions` map keeps only non-zero versions. Empty `facts` and `factsVersions` objects are preserved. If no input has those keys, they are omitted.
  - Top-level key order is fixed: `lockFileVersion`, `registryFileHashes`, `selectedYankedVersions`, `moduleExtensions`, then `facts`, then `factsVersions`. Nested keys are sorted lexicographically after splitting on `:`, so `//:rbe_extensions.bzl%…` precedes `//python/extensions:python.bzl` which precedes `…/private:internal_deps.bzl`, and `os:linux,arch:aarch64` precedes `os:linux,arch:amd64`. Fact ids and keys sort the same way (`bar`, `baz`, `foo`; `cbor`, `json`, `xml`).
  - The lockfile shape is jq-pretty JSON only. The identity merge must match `src/test/tools/bzlmod/MODULE.bazel.lock` byte for byte. The test never uses a Starlark lockfile.
  - Zel's only merge-related behavior is on a failed parse: if the text contains `<<<<<<<` or `>>>>>>>`, the error adds "This looks like a merge conflict. See https://bazel.build/external/lockfile#merge-conflicts for advice." That does not merge. Its writer uses `BTreeMap` string order (not split on `:`) and always emits `facts` and `factsVersions`.

### `scripts/release/relnotes.sh`

- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - Zel has no `scripts/release/` tree and no `relnotes.sh` or `relnotes.py`. It does not generate Bazel-style release notes. Vendored changelog helpers under `third_party/bcr/` are dependency packaging, not a zel release-notes generator.
  - Non-rolling releases (`is_rolling_release` prints `0`) call `python3 ${RELNOTES_SCRIPT_DIR}/relnotes.py` with no arguments. The shell does not pass a range, baseline, or tags. Python reads `HEAD`: a `release-*` branch name (with `rcN` stripped) or `git describe --tags`. It lists `git tag --sort=refname`, drops tags containing `pre`, appends the current version if it is not already a tag, and takes the previous sorted tag as the last release. The range is `git merge-base HEAD <that tag>` through `HEAD`, minus notes that also appear from that merge-base to the previous tag. The shell prints that stdout unchanged, optionally wrapped by a delimiter. The unquoted script path is word-split only if the directory contains IFS or glob characters.
  - Rolling releases (`…-pre.YYYYMMDD.N`, function prints `1`) stay in bash. The revision baseline is `git merge-base master <branch>` (default `HEAD`). Cherry-picks are commits on `baseline..branch` whose `git patch-id` is missing from `baseline..master`. A match is replaced by the master hash. That list is only printed as “Cherry picks” via `__create_revision_information`. `create_release_notes` ignores the baseline and cherry-pick arguments it is given.
  - Note selection reads `Baseline: <hash>` from `git show master:CHANGELOG.md`, plus following ` + <hash>:` lines until a blank line. `echo $BASELINE $CHERRY_PICKS` and `__release_notes ${last_release}` word-split that into separate words, then only the first word is kept. The git range is `${baseline}..` (through `HEAD`). Changelog cherry-picks are not passed into `__get_release_notes_commits`, so they are not excluded. Rollbacks matching `^Rollback of commit <hash>.$` are excluded. `RELNOTES` / `RELNOTES[NEW]` / `RELNOTES[INC]` lines are kept unless the text is `none`, `n/a`, `no`, or `.`.
  - Notes are stored with `eval "RELNOTES_${kind}+=(\"\${relnote_text}\")"`. A `"`, `\`, backtick, or `$` in the text is parsed again and can change or drop the note. Bash `=~` anchors to the whole string, so a multi-line `RELNOTES` body fails the match and is dropped. `fold -s -w 66` wraps on spaces and strips trailing spaces. Command substitution strips trailing newlines. `__trim_empty_lines` swaps newlines for form feeds, so a form feed in a note is corrupted, and lines starting with `#` are removed before the notes are written back.

### `src/java_tools/junitrunner/java/com/google/testing/coverage/BitField.java`
- Bazel lines: 215
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - Zel has no `com.google.testing.coverage.BitField`. The nearest coverage code is the vendored Java report merger under `zel-cursor/crates/zel-bazel-tools/resources/tools/test/CoverageOutputGenerator/java/com/google/devtools/coverageoutputgenerator/`, which stores branch hits as maps, not probe bit fields.
  - Storage is a cloned `byte[]`. The constructor and `getBytes()` both clone, so the caller cannot alias the buffer. `sizeInBits()` is `bytes.length * 8`.
  - Bit order is least-significant-bit first inside each byte: `byteIndex = index / 8`, `bitIndex = index % 8`, `mask = 1 << bitIndex`. Java `/` and `%` truncate toward zero. A negative `index` yields a negative `byteIndex` (`ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` or `NegativeArraySizeException` on grow). An index past the end of `isBitSet` returns false instead of throwing.
  - `setBit` grows with `Arrays.copyOf`, which zero-fills. `clearBit` uses the same path with the bit cleared.
  - `and` returns a new field whose length is the minimum of the two lengths, so bits past the shorter field are dropped. `or` returns a new field whose length is the maximum and ORs the shorter prefix into a copy of the longer array. The `or` Javadoc says it returns `this`; the method returns a new `BitField`.
  - `equals(Object)` and `equals(byte[])` are `Arrays.equals` on the raw bytes, so trailing zero bytes make two fields unequal even when the set bits in the shared prefix match. `hashCode` is `Arrays.hashCode(bytes)` (Java's 31-polynomial over the signed bytes). The `byte[]` overload does not override `equals(Object)`.
  - `countBitsSet` uses a 256-entry popcount table filled by `BIT_COUNT_LOOKUP[i] = popcount(i/2)` and `BIT_COUNT_LOOKUP[i+1] = that + 1`. Java `byte` is signed, so the lookup index is `0xFF & b`. Using the raw negative byte as an index throws `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`.
  - `not` inverts each byte with `Integer.valueOf(~bytes[i]).byteValue()`. The `byte` is sign-extended to `int` before `~`; `byteValue()` keeps the low 8 bits, which is still a per-byte invert. `any` is true when any byte is nonzero, including a negative byte whose high bit is set.

### `src/java_tools/junitrunner/java/com/google/testing/junit/runner/util/XmlEscapers.java`
- Bazel lines: 141
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-query/src/format.rs` (`xml_escape_attr`) and `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-exec/src/test_runner.rs` (`synthesize_xml`)
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - Bazel builds two escapers from one map. Shared rules: `&` `<` `>` become `&amp;` `&lt;` `&gt;`; every C0 control in `U+0000`–`U+001F` except tab, LF, and CR becomes the literal character U+FFFD (not a character reference and not deleted). The content escaper stops there, so `'`, `"`, tab, LF, and CR are copied raw (`XmlWriter.writeCharacters`). The attribute escaper adds `'` → `&apos;`, `"` → `&quot;`, tab → `&#x9;`, LF → `&#xA;`, CR → `&#xD;` (uppercase hex, no leading zeros). `XmlWriter.writeAttribute` then wraps that result in single quotes, so the apostrophe escape is required for well-formedness.
  - Query XML only has attribute escaping, and only inside double quotes (` {k}="{escaped}"`). There is no content escaper. `'` is left raw. Tab, LF, and CR become decimal `&#9;` `&#10;` `&#13;`, not `&#x9;` `&#xA;` `&#xD;`. Every other scalar below `U+0020`, including NUL, becomes `&#N;` (decimal). Bazel replaces those controls with U+FFFD in both content and attributes.
  - `synthesize_xml` uses one replacer for attribute text (`name`, `message`): only `&` `<` `>` `"`. Apostrophes, tab, LF, CR, and other C0 controls stay literal inside double-quoted attributes, so a newline or NUL in a name or message is not escaped. The log is not passed through a content escaper; it is placed in CDATA after only splitting `]]>` into `]]>]]&gt;<![CDATA[`. Characters illegal in XML 1.0 Char (C0 controls other than tab/LF/CR) therefore remain in the CDATA, where Bazel’s content escaper would have written U+FFFD. `&` and `<` inside the log are also left raw, which CDATA allows and the content escaper would not.
  - UTF-16: Bazel’s `CharEscaper.escape` walks Java `char` code units. The safe range is inclusive `U+0000` through `U+FFFD`; only `U+FFFE` and `U+FFFF` fall outside it and each becomes one U+FFFD. Surrogates `U+D800`–`U+DFFF` are inside the safe range and have no explicit replacement, so supplementary characters and unpaired surrogates are copied unchanged. U+FFFD itself is safe and is not rewritten. Neither Zel function maps `U+FFFE` or `U+FFFF` to U+FFFD. Zel iterates Unicode scalars (`str::chars`), so it cannot preserve or pass through an unpaired surrogate the way the Java escaper does.

Surrogates sit inside the safe range ending at U+FFFD, so a well-formed pair is written through as one 4-byte UTF-8 sequence. This test never supplies a surrogate. ### `src/java_tools/singlejar/java/com/google/devtools/build/singlejar/ZipEntryFilter.java`
- Bazel lines: 128
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - Bazel defines a thread-safe `ZipEntryFilter` whose `accept(String filename, StrategyCallback callback)` decides, once per unique entry name, how every entry of that name is combined. Zel has no singlejar filter type.
  - `accept` is documented to be called exactly once per name. A rename is the exception: the original name is not treated as already encountered.
  - `StrategyCallback` requires exactly one of `skip`, `copy`, `rename`, or `customMerge` per name. A second call throws `IllegalStateException`. The callback may defer the work.
  - `skip()` drops the current entry and every later entry with the same name.
  - `copy(Date date)` keeps the first entry, drops later duplicates, and overwrites the entry timestamp when `date` is non-null.
  - `rename(String filename, Date date)` stores the first entry under a new name, drops later entries of the original name, and overwrites the timestamp when `date` is non-null.
  - `customMerge(Date date, CustomMergeStrategy strategy)` merges every entry of that name with one strategy instance. The same strategy object must not be passed twice. A non-null `date` sets the output timestamp; a null `date` means the current time.
  - `merge(InputStream, OutputStream)` is called for each same-named entry, then `finish(OutputStream)` writes the single merged entry once. Each instance given to `customMerge` is not called from two threads at once.
  - `skipEmpty()` defaults to `false`, so an empty merge result is still written. Returning `true` skips that empty result.

- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-util/src/lib.rs` (`md5`)
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - Padding matches RFC 1321: `0x80`, zeros until the length is 56 mod 64, then the 64-bit bit-length. Block words and the length suffix are little-endian in both. The low 64 bits of the bit length match.
  - Hex of a finished digest matches: lowercase encoding of A, B, C, and D as little-endian bytes. Empty, `"abc"`, and the quick-brown-fox vectors are the RFC values.
  - Raw `Finish(unsigned char digest[16])` copies `state[0..3]` as host-endian `uint32_t`s with no `htole32`. Zel’s 16-byte digest is always little-endian. They match on little-endian hosts. On big-endian, `Finish` disagrees with both Zel and Bazel’s own `String()`. `md5.h` defines `htole32(x)` as `(x)` on Apple and Windows under a little-endian CPU assumption.
  - `String()` is `const` and does not pad or run `Finish`. It hex-encodes only blocks already passed through `Transform`. Zel `hex_digest` always pads, so a buffered partial block differs until `Finish`.
  - Zel is one-shot. Bazel streams via `Update` and `Reset`. `count` is a byte counter (the header comment says bits). `Transform` then adds the padding length into `count`, so the object is not a clean finalized digest if reused.
  - Round functions, shifts, K, the index schedule, and the IVs match. Bazel writes `F` as `z ^ (x & (y ^ z))` and `G` as `F(z, x, y)`. Zel uses the RFC forms. The constants are the same.
  - A byte-identical copy of this file is vendored under `zel-bazel-tools`. `zel-exec` digest functions are SHA-1/256/384/512 and BLAKE3, not MD5.

### `src/main/cpp/util/numbers.cc`
- Bazel lines: 215
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-options/src/startup.rs` (`safe_strto32`)
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - The vendored `.cc` matches Bazel. Zel does not run that file. `safe_strto32` is reimplemented only for startup range checks. `strto32` has no port.
  - `safe_strto32` is base 10 only. The digit table encodes letters as `0-35`, but both digit loops reject `digit >= 10`, so `"0x10"` fails and `"010"` is decimal 10. Zel’s startup parser agrees on that grammar.
  - One optional `+` or `-` is accepted after leading space. Both accept `i32::MIN` and `i32::MAX`. Bazel reaches `INT_MIN` by subtracting digits instead of negating a positive value. A second sign, a space between the sign and the digits, whitespace-only, and a bare `+` or `-` fail both.
  - On overflow Bazel writes `INT_MAX` or `INT_MIN` and returns false. An invalid digit writes the partial value. Zel returns `None` and does not saturate. Startup call sites only use the value when the parse succeeds, so the five range checks match on accept and reject.
  - Trailing ASCII space fails both. An embedded NUL differs: Bazel’s `c_str()` stops at the first NUL (`"123\0xyz"` succeeds as 123). Zel rejects the NUL byte.
  - `strto32` is `strtol` plus a clamp. Base `0` uses `strtol`’s `0x` and leading-zero rules. Trailing junk is left in `endptr` and is not an error. `GetTerminalColumns` accepts any result whose `endptr` is at the NUL, including a clamped `INT_MAX` and a negative value, and it ignores `errno`.
  - Zel’s `$COLUMNS` path is `parse::<usize>()` with a `> 0` filter, base 10 only. It rejects leading whitespace (`" 80"`; `strtol` accepts it), rejects a leading `-`, rejects a value that does not fit in `usize`, and accepts values above `i32::MAX` that fit in `usize`. Bazel clamps those to `2147483647` and still uses them.
  - Bazel `GetServerPid` uses `safe_strto32`, which rejects a trailing newline. Zel `read_pid` uses `trim().parse()`, which strips both ends, including Unicode whitespace.

### `src/main/cpp/util/path.cc`
- Bazel lines: 52
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-bazel-tools/resources/src/main/cpp/util/path.cc`
- Verdict: match
- Differences:
  - The resource copy is the same 52 lines. `Dirname` and `Basename` forward to `SplitPath`. `JoinPath` is a four-way `/` join and does not normalize. `\` is never a separator here.
  - `JoinPath("", x)` returns `x`. `JoinPath("foo/", "/bar")` drops one leading `/` from the second argument. `JoinPath("foo/", "//bar")` drops only that one character (`"foo//bar"`). An empty child still adds `/`. `.` and `..` are left in place.
  - Zel’s live joiner is `PathFragment`, not this `.cc`. `get_relative` returns the child when the child is absolute or the parent is empty, and returns the parent when the child is empty. `JoinPath` never replaces a non-empty parent.
  - `PathFragment::create` rewrites `\` to `/`, drops empty and `.` segments, pops `..` (absolute `..` cannot escape the root), and accepts a drive (`c:` / `c:/` becomes `C:/` with length 3). `foo` plus `bar/../baz` becomes `foo/baz`. `create("//foo")` is `/foo`. `JoinPath` does none of this.
  - Normalized fragments do not keep a trailing `/` except the root prefix. `Dirname("foo/bar/")` is `foo/bar` with an empty basename. `create("foo/bar/")` is already `foo/bar`, so the parent is `foo` and the basename is `bar`.

### `src/main/cpp/workspace_layout.cc`
- Bazel lines: 87
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-client/src/lib.rs`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - Both take the nearest ancestor that contains a boundary file. Bazel’s set, in order, is `MODULE.bazel`, `REPO.bazel`, `WORKSPACE.bazel`, and `WORKSPACE`. Zel also treats `MODULE.zel` and `WORKSPACE.zel` as boundaries, so a tree with only those files is a workspace in Zel and not in Bazel.
  - Bazel counts a marker only when it exists and is not a directory (`stat`, symlinks followed). A directory, or a symlink to a directory, with one of those names is ignored. Zel’s `exists` does not reject directories, so a directory named `WORKSPACE` or `MODULE.bazel` makes that directory the workspace root.
  - Bazel’s walk stops before testing the filesystem root. A marker in `/` is found only when the cwd is `/`. Zel’s parent walk checks `/` (and a Windows drive root), so a marker at the filesystem root makes every path under it a workspace.
  - Bazel calls `GetWorkspace` on `GetCanonicalCwd()` (`realpath` of the cwd). Zel walks the `PathFragment` it is given. `main` passes `current_dir()` with no extra `realpath`, and `PathFragment::create` only collapses `.` and `..` lexically, so a cwd that still contains a symlink can land on a different root.
  - `GetWorkspace` returns `""` outside a workspace. `find_workspace_root_opt` returns `None`. `find_workspace_root`, used for Bazelisk planning, falls back to the cwd, so that search still runs when Bazel has an empty workspace.
  - `GetPrettyWorkspaceName` is `Basename(workspace)`, used as the server process title `bazel(<basename>)`. Zel never renames the server process that way.
  - `GetWorkspaceRcPath` always returns `<workspace>/tools/bazel.rc` and ignores `startup_args`. Zel has no `tools/bazel.rc` path. Workspace rc loading reads `<workspace>/.bazelrc`.
  - `ResolveWorkspaceRelativeRcFilePath` requires the prefix `%workspace%/` (the trailing slash is part of the prefix) and returns nullopt when that path does not exist. Zel matches any string that starts with `%workspace%`, including `%workspace%` with no slash and `%workspace%foo`. Bazel still joins onto an empty workspace string, which yields the relative remainder.
  - `ensure_repo_boundary` looks for the same four Bazel names on an external repo and, when the directory is not itself a symlink, creates an empty `REPO.bazel`. The C++ client only detects a workspace. It does not create a boundary file.

A spawn that inputs one of its own actual outputs blocks itself and is never written, and any spawn that stays blocked on an unemitted spawn is silently dropped. Zel writes every logged spawn.

A stateless exponential `min(initial * multiplier^attempt, max) * (1 + jitter * r)` is slept, with `r` from `subsec_nanos % 2001` (default 100ms, multiplier 2, jitter 0.1, max 5s, 5 retries), and every `run` starts at attempt 0. The exponent is `powi(attempt as i32)`, so an attempt above `i32::MAX` wraps the exponent negative and the delay collapses instead of staying at the cap.

### `src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/remote/grpc/SharedConnectionFactory.java`

Blocking is later, in HTTP/2 `open_stream`, against the peer’s `MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS` (initially `u32::MAX`), and the slot follows the stream rather than an explicit handle close.

Zel uses `str::len()` (UTF-8 bytes), so non-ASCII names cross 255 on a different side. The digest is SHA-256 of `hashString(..., UTF_8)`, which UTF-8-encodes those Latin-1 units (bytes ≥ 0x80 expand to two UTF-8 bytes). Zel hashes the string’s UTF-8 bytes. Non-UTF-8 filesystem names are turned into U+FFFD by `to_string_lossy` before mangling.

Zel registers the action for any artifact and never runs that regex.
  - `PathFragment.getRelative` leaves an empty solib directory or an absolute link path unchanged and normalizes `.`, `..`, and repeated separators. Zel concatenates `{solib_dir}/{rest}` as raw text, so an empty directory becomes a leading `/` and `.` / `..` / `//` stay in the soname and the output path. `getDynamicLibrarySoname` sees the normalized fragment; Zel uses the caller string.
  - Omitted `preserve_name` and `prefix_consumer` default to false, and a missing or non-string `runtime_solib_dir_base` falls back to `solib_directory`. Bazel requires those Starlark arguments; a Java `null` runtime dir selects the toolchain directory. Non-booleans are accepted through `is_truthy()`.

Zel deletes the output first, and if `symlink` fails it copies the target bytes. There is no spawn-log failure and no metadata injection. `getProgressMessage()` is null; Zel’s symlink execution path reports `Creating symlink …`. `mayInsensitivelyPropagateInputs()` is true, and Zel has no case-insensitive rewind propagation.

### `src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/sandbox/AsynchronousTreeDeleter.java`
- Bazel lines: 133
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - No async trash mover. Bazel no-ops when the path is missing, otherwise renames it to `trashBase/<n>` (`n` from an `AtomicInteger` starting at 0, decimal, wrapping through negative `int` values) and deletes that path on a background pool. A failed rename deletes the original tree synchronously and does not enqueue. Failures of the background delete are swallowed.

Negative millis use Java toward-zero `/` and `%`, which can make `tv_nsec` negative.

Rust stores that as `None` and leaves the option out of the parsed map, so readers see absence rather than null or an empty list. Other defaults are not installed unless the flag is set; Java’s effective value is the converted default. Repeatable occurrences concatenate list-valued converter results in both.
  - A non-empty `deprecationWarning` is the only deprecation signal Rust emits, and only for `--name` argv tokens (not abbreviations). Java also warns for a `@Deprecated` field with an empty warning string (`Option '<name>' is deprecated`, no extra text) and skips the warning at invocation-policy priority. Rust `is_deprecated()` checks `OptionMetadataTag::Deprecated`, which is not Java’s `@Deprecated` check.

### `src/main/java/com/google/devtools/common/options/OptionValueDescription.java`
- Bazel lines: 493
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-options/src/definition.rs`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - Zel keeps one record per option (raw strings, one value, one priority, one source) and never builds the default, single, repeatable, expansion, or implicit-requirements trackers. Unset options are omitted instead of a default description whose value is the converted default, whose source and canonical instances are null, and whose `addOptionInstance` throws `IllegalStateException` (`Cannot add values to the default option value...`). The Java `ConstructionException` strings for the wrong tracker are never thrown. A conversion failure only fails the parse; there is no `containsErrors` flag that makes `getParsedOptions` fall back to the default.
  - Single-value flags still replace the previous value when the new priority is greater or equal, but none of the conflict warnings are emitted: implicitly defined by both parents, an implicit value overriding a previous one, a new value overriding an implicit setting, a command-line expansion overriding an explicit option, or an option expanded from two parents (including the same-category `RC_FILE` case, which Java suppresses).
  - Repeatable values are appended in encounter order and kept under one source string. Java orders the effective value, the distinct sources joined by `", "`, and the canonical instances by `OptionPriority`, flattens a converter `List`, and drops instances with an implicit dependent. The startup parser pushes the converted value without flattening, so a list-valued converter is nested.
  - Expansion options still store their own converted value and can be recorded as a canonical flag when they are not `Void`. Java's value and source are null, canonical instances are empty, a non-empty supplied value warns that it is ignored (`... is an expansion option. It does not accept values... Value '...' will be ignored.`), and the bundle source is `expanded from <option>` or `expanded from <option> (source <source>)`. Zel's child parses record source `"command line"`, and `merge` replaces any existing value with no priority check.
  - Implicit requirements run for every definition that lists them, including one that also has an expansion, at `ComputedDefault`, and before the parent is stored. A requirement that names the parent therefore loses to the explicit command-line value. Java handles them only on the implicit-requirements subtype, after the single-value update, at child priority (higher than the parent, so the requirement wins), with source `implicit requirement of <option>` or `implicit requirement of <option> (source <source>)`, and warns when the explicit value equals the default (`... sets <option> to its default value. ... this options expands to {...}.`). Because `merge` overwrites unconditionally, a requirement also replaces a higher-priority value of another flag.

### `src/main/native/windows/processes-jni.cc`
- Bazel lines: 570
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-ffi-bridge/src/native.rs`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - Zel `process` is Unix-only (`cfg(unix)`): current pid, parent pid, `kill` 0/15/9, nice, rusage, and CPU count. It does not create a child, wire stdin/stdout/stderr, wait, or read an exit code. The same file lists Windows as unimplemented.
  - `createProcess` always returns a `NativeProcess` pointer. A failed `Create` is a sticky wide-string error read later by `processGetLastError` and then cleared. Zel returns `io::Result` immediately and has no clearable last-error string.
  - A null Java string becomes an empty `wstring`. A null env `jbyteArray` means inherit. An env block must be at least 4 bytes and end in 4 zero bytes or creation fails. Empty stdout/stderr redirects mean pipes. Zel has no null-vs-empty path or env-block checks.
  - Paths are Java UTF-16 copied as `WCHAR`, `/` is rewritten to `\`, and redirects gain a `\\?\` prefix unless empty, `NUL`, or already UNC. Two non-empty redirects share one handle when `_wcsnicmp` matches. `redirectErrorStream` duplicates the stdout handle onto stderr and ignores the stderr path. Zel paths are raw Unix bytes with no slash rewrite, UNC prefix, or case-insensitive redirect merge.
  - Stdout/stderr files are `CreateFileW` `GENERIC_WRITE`, `FILE_SHARE_READ`, `OPEN_ALWAYS`, then seek to `FILE_END`. Pipes are 65536 bytes with inheritable child ends. Read/write bounds errors and I/O errors return `-1`. A broken pipe or a closed stream returns 0. `Close` calls `CancelIoEx` then `CloseHandle`. Zel has none of this stream or append-redirect behavior.
  - `waitFor` takes an `int64` timeout. Negative means infinite. It returns `0` success, `1` timeout, `2` error, and on success or timeout `WaitableProcess::WaitFor` terminates the process and its job with exit code 130 before returning. `getExitCode` returns `259` (`STILL_ACTIVE`) while running, the process code after exit, or `-1` if the query fails, all as `jint`. `getProcessPid` casts `DWORD` to `jint`, so pids above `2^31-1` wrap negative. `streamBytesAvailable` returns a `DWORD` as `jint`. Zel uses `u32` pids and `io::Result`, with no `259` sentinel, no `0`/`1`/`2` wait codes, and terminate is `SIGTERM` to one pid (`kill_hard` is `SIGKILL`) without a job object or exit code 130.
  - Error text is a Windows `wchar` message returned as a Java UTF-16 string. Zel surfaces `io::Error` as UTF-8.

### `src/main/native/windows/sleep_prevention_jni.cc`
- Bazel lines: 59
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - Bazel keeps a process-wide `std::atomic_int` sleep stack starting at 0. The first `pushDisableSleep` calls `SetThreadExecutionState(ES_CONTINUOUS | ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED | ES_AWAYMODE_REQUIRED)`; later pushes only increment. `popDisableSleep` decrements and, when the count returns to 0, calls `SetThreadExecutionState(ES_CONTINUOUS)`. Both calls always return `0`. A pop that drives the count below 0 hits `assert` (abort when asserts are enabled). Zel never calls `SetThreadExecutionState` and has no push/pop sleep-prevention API.

After a successful base64 decode, a binary parse failure still falls through to the text parser; Java only does that when base64 decoding throws `IllegalArgumentException`.

### `src/main/starlark/builtins_bzl/common/xcode/providers.bzl`
- Bazel lines: 173

Java `DottedVersion.equals` follows `compareTo`, where trailing zero components and a missing second number do not count.
  - Ordering keeps the whole non-digit tail as one string. Java splits each component with `(?i)\d+([a-z0-9]*?)?(\d+)?` and compares that trailing integer as a signed 32-bit value, so `1.2beta12 > 1.2beta2` and `1.2beta == 1.2beta0`. Zel orders `1.2beta12 < 1.2beta2` and treats `1.2beta` and `1.2beta0` as unequal.
  - Java stops at a trailing descriptive component matching `(?i)[a-z]\w*`, so `10.10.simulator.internal` equals `10.10`. Zel keeps those components, and a non-empty tail sorts before a bare number.
  - Java `Integer.parseInt` rejects a component above `2^31-1` and rejects `1..2`, `2:3`, and `1.-1`. Zel parses with `u64` (`unwrap_or(0)` on overflow) and accepts those strings when the first character is a digit. `None` becomes `None` instead of the Java `String` type error, so init does not fail and the getters return `None`.
  - Returned objects have `.version` and no `.to_string`. Bazel’s Starlark field is `.to_string` (`compare_to` exists on both).
  - `availability.lower()` is Rust Unicode `to_lowercase` (a character can expand, as with `İ`). Bazel uses `Ascii.toLowerCase` (ASCII `A–Z` only). `LOCAL` / `REMOTE` / `BOTH` / `UNKNOWN` still match.
  - `xcode_version_flag.find("-")` and the slice that builds `requires-xcode-label:` count Unicode scalars. Bazel `String.indexOf` / `substring` count UTF-16 code units, so a non-BMP character before `-` changes the label.

### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/actions/ActionCacheCheckerTest.java`

Zel keeps no hit/miss counters. `must_execute` returns `DifferentActionKey`, `DifferentEnvironment`, `OutputsMissing`, `DifferentDeps`, or `DifferentFiles`, in that order, so a missing output is reported before an input-set or content change.
  - Any must-execute miss that already had an entry removes it before the action runs. An expired remote file, an expired tree child, an expired archived representation, a flipped `useArchivedTreeArtifacts` flag, or a metadata-disabled recheck of a missing output leaves `cache.get` null. Zel keeps the previous entry until a later successful `put_entry` or a failed execution.
  - `actionExecutionSalt` and the output permission mode are inside the cache digest. Zel’s action key and `must_execute` ignore both. Client env is only `getClientEnvironmentVariables()` (unused vars stay hits) for every action. Zel hashes `SpawnAction.inherited_env` names that exist in the client env, and file-write and other non-spawn actions ignore the client env.
  - With `storeOutputMetadata`, the entry stores remote file metadata and tree metadata (remote children only, remote archived file, resolved path) and a hit injects that metadata into the output store while the output path is absent. Local file and local archived metadata are omitted. An empty tree is a hit with no directory. A matching local tree child or archived file stays a hit and the injected value mixes local metadata for paths that exist with remote metadata for the rest. Zel stores local content-digest strings, treats a missing path as `OutputsMissing`, and does not inject remote, tree, archived, or resolved-path metadata. A remote-only output that is never created fails in Zel as “output was not created” (exit 1, entry removed) unless it is pending, and a pending missing output still cannot hit.
  - `OutputChecker.shouldTrustMetadata` false is a `DIGEST_MISMATCH`. `CHECK_TTL` rejects metadata whose expiration is missing or not after now, including one expired tree child or an expired archived representation, and drops the entry. Zel has no trust callback and no expiration.
  - Proxy outputs are recorded on the entry. A later check with null metadata in the store calls `ProxyMetadataFactory`: equal proxy metadata is a hit and is injected; a different proxy, a null return, or an `IOException` is a `DIGEST_MISMATCH` and the proxy path remains on the entry. Zel has no proxy-output set and no factory.
  - `CONSTANT_METADATA` outputs are compared as constant metadata when the file is readable, so only deletion (metadata `IOException` becomes null) forces a re-execution. Zel always hashes file bytes, so a content change misses as well.

### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/actions/ResourceManagerTest.java`
- Bazel lines: 958

  - The test manager leaves `allow_one_action_on_resource_unavailable` unset, so an idle over-budget acquire throws `UserExecException`. Zel defaults `allow_one_when_unavailable` to true and `acquire` never fails: it admits the request when nothing is active, otherwise it waits on a condvar.
  - CPU admission charges the full amount already held but only requires 0.6× the new request, so 0.5+0.6 succeeds and 0.099 then 0.99 succeeds while 0.99 then 0.099 stays blocked. Zel requires `used + requested <= available` in both orders, so both pairs block once any action is running.

  - An unknown extra resource throws `UserExecException` before waiting. Zel treats a missing key as capacity 0, so it is admitted while idle with allow-one on, or waited on forever otherwise.
  - Waiters sit in three deques, served LOCAL, then DYNAMIC_WORKER, then DYNAMIC_STANDALONE, LIFO within a priority, and a later smaller request can run while an earlier larger one stays queued. Zel `notify_all` has no priority and no LIFO.
  - An interrupted acquire drops its waiter, so a later `setAvailableResources` does not leave that request holding RAM. Zel does not observe interruption or a cancellable queue.
  - `threadHasResources` is thread-local. Zel does not track it.
  - A worker-keyed acquire borrows a pool worker, and `invalidateAndClose` maps `InterruptedException`, `IOException`, `UserExecException` (`NO_RESPONSE`), and null onto the corresponding `PENDING_KILL_DUE_TO_*` worker statuses. Zel only counts CPU, RAM, extra resources, and test slots, and releases them on drop.
  - CPU-load scheduling blocks on the 5s window estimate plus measured load, `windowUpdate` clears that window, and a fourth concurrent 1-CPU action is refused at 3× available CPU even when measured load is 0.1. After a window clear and load 0.1, another 1-CPU action is admitted while 1 CPU is already charged. Zel's flag only refuses when something is active and charged CPU is already at the cap, still requires `used + requested <= available`, and has no load sample, window, or 3× cap.

### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/actions/cache/CompactPersistentActionCacheTest.java`
- Bazel lines: 775
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-exec/src/action_cache.rs`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - Bazel `size()` counts a validation record (key `-10`, a 4-byte big-endian indexer size). One `put` makes `size()` 2; `remove` of that key leaves 1; `clear` leaves 0. Zel `len()` counts user entries only (1 after one put, 0 after remove) and writes no validation record.
  - Bazel persists six files (`action_cache.blaze`, `action_journal.blaze`, `filename_index.blaze`, `filename_index_journal.blaze`, `timestamp.blaze`, `timestamp_journal.blaze`). `save` keeps the journal when `journalSize * 100 < cacheSize` (byte lengths): two puts after a 300-entry full save stay in the journal, and ten further puts force a full save that deletes it. A later incremental save still reloads the earlier journal keys. Zel `save_to_disk` always rewrites one `ZELACv1` file with an 8-byte SHA-1 trailer, so there is no journal and no incremental reload.
  - Bazel `clear()` full-saves an empty map, so a new `create` on the same root has size 0. Zel `clear` only empties the in-memory map.
  - Bazel `create` deletes every cache-root child outside those six names. Zel load leaves extra files in place.
  - Bazel splits load failure by file and error class. The ISO-8859-1 bytes `incompatible` on any of the six files are an incompatible format: the cache root is deleted, `corruptedCacheRoot` is absent, the event handler is not called, and size is 0. A map file shortened by one byte is corruption: the root is renamed onto `corruptedCacheRoot`, a warning event is reported, and the reloaded cache is empty. A journal shortened by one byte is dropped: no event, no quarantine, and the map remains (size 301 = 300 entries plus the validation record). Zel treats a bad magic, a short file, a checksum mismatch, and a different digest-function name the same way: an empty map, `load_warning` set, and the file left in place.
  - Bazel stores last access as a signed 32-bit count of epoch minutes. `put` records `clock.now()`, `get` refreshes that timestamp, and `remove` / `removeIf` delete only that key’s timestamp. The map round-trips (the test’s 100-day steps from the epoch stay on minute boundaries, through 700 days). Zel entries have no timestamps, and `get` does not change access time.
  - Bazel `trim(threshold, maxAge)` drops entries strictly older than `now - maxAge` when `numStale != 0` and `numStale < threshold * actionMap.size()` is false. `actionMap.size()` includes the validation record, and the multiply is `float` (`0.2f * 5` is `1.0f`, so one stale entry of five is removed; `0.3f` keeps it). Threshold `0` removes every stale entry. The kept set is saved and reloaded. Zel has no trim.
  - Bazel `removeIf(Entry::discoversInputs)` removes entries whose discovered-input list is non-null, including an empty list, and the next full save persists that. Zel stores `discovered_inputs` as a `Vec<String>` and has no predicate removal, so an empty list cannot mean “does not discover inputs.”
  - Bazel `put`/`get` round-trips remote file metadata (digest, size, location index, expiration epoch millis or `-1` if absent, in-memory flag, optional resolved path), tree metadata with remote children only, a remote archived file only (local children and a local archived file are omitted), the tree resolved path, and proxy outputs as exec-path strings. Local file metadata is omitted, so `getOutputFile` is null. `discoversInputs` is part of the persisted entry (`toString` differs for true vs false). Zel stores an action-key string, a client-env digest, a metadata digest, a path-to-digest `BTreeMap`, and a discovered-path list. The simple `put` updates only `action_key`.

  - `flaky = 2` fails in Bazel with `expected one of [False, True, 0, 1]`. Zel reports `expected value of type 'bool' for attribute 'flaky'`. `flaky = 1` is still flaky, and the default is not.
  - `--noexpand_test_suites` leaves the suite as the analyzed target. The aspect label set is `@@//:suite` plus every implicit test, or `@@//:suite` plus only the explicit `tests`. Zel always expands the suite and drops it, so the suite label is absent and the flag does not change the aspect roots. Default expansion (members only, suite omitted) matches.
  - A non-executable `--coverage_report_generator` fails analysis with `--coverage_report_generator does not refer to an executable target`. Zel ignores a label that has no executable and uses the default LCOV merger.
  - With the legacy test toolchain the test action’s execution platform is the first extra execution platform (`//:linux_x86_64_exec`, exec properties `os=linux`, `cpu=x86_64`) for every target os/cpu. With the default test toolchain it is the platform whose constraints match the target. If none match, analysis still succeeds, the action falls back to the first execution platform, and the unrunnable reason is `No matching toolchain found for type …//tools/test:default_test_toolchain_type, which is required to run tests for target platform …`. Zel has no test-toolchain selection and no that reason string.
  - `testing.ExecutionInfo` with `exec_group = "custom_group"` puts `custom_group.key` on the test action as `key=good` and leaves `test.key` off. `--use_target_platform_for_tests` runs the action on the target platform and keeps only that platform’s exec properties (`key2=good` from `//:linux_aarch64`), dropping the rule’s `key` and the host platform’s properties. Zel records the flag and does not apply it.
  - `--run_under=//:run_under_tool` is built for the `test` exec group’s platform (`//:linux`) while the test action runs on the `ExecutionInfo` group (`//:android`) and the test binary is built for the rule’s `exec_compatible_with` (`//:macos`). Zel resolves `--run_under` to the executable already configured for the test and does not give the tool that exec-group transition.
  - The test command’s execution OS is the test action’s platform: `OS.DARWIN` when the `test` exec group requires macOS, and `OS.LINUX` when `ExecutionInfo` selects an exec group that requires Linux, even if the target platform is Windows. Zel does not set that execution OS.

### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/authandtls/credentialhelper/CredentialHelperTest.java`

  - A 63 KiB header is read only after the process exits, so the pipe must hold it or the call deadlocks and times out. Zel drains stdout while the process runs, so a payload larger than the pipe buffer does not deadlock.

Zel acknowledges every decoded request immediately and sends status 0 only after the client ends the stream, including when the last event is not stream-finished.
  - Acknowledgements can be held and later flushed FIFO, then the current event’s acknowledgement is appended and the buffer is replaced. The default is to send immediately. Zel never batches an earlier acknowledgement onto a later response.
  - Each acknowledgement copies the request stream id and sequence. A switch instead acknowledges sequence + 1 and skips the normal status path. Zel always echoes the request sequence and omits `stream_id` when that field is absent.
  - Lifecycle events, all tool events, and successfully acknowledged tool events are kept in insertion order per stream id. Zel keeps two global arrival-order byte lists, with no per-stream split and no separate success list.
  - The inbound tool-stream failure is stored as a status that stays null until then; tests accept `CANCELLED` or `INTERNAL`. Zel does not retain that status.
  - The recorder binds a freshly chosen TCP port and reports -1 when no server is running. Zel uses an in-memory duplex and has no port.

A non-completing last event (and a close with no completing event) is `UNKNOWN_STATUS`; exit code 0 is `COMMAND_SUCCEEDED` and any other `BuildCompletingEvent` exit is `COMMAND_FAILED`. Zel has only those two results, defaults to succeeded, and does not derive status from the last event. Tool-stream sequence 1 carries the raw keyword set and `checkPrecedingLifecycleEvents=false`. Zel rewrites keywords to `command_name=`, `protocol_name=BEP`, and `user_keyword=`, puts them on every lifecycle RPC including invocation-finished, and forces `check_preceding_lifecycle_events_present` true.

Zel retries that unary call and then discards the error, still uploads the tool stream, and still publishes finish events after a successful stream.

Zel does not treat `CANCELLED` as retriable, so that stream fails on the first response. A successful ack resets the retry counter, so 13 events that each fail once with `UNAVAILABLE` still complete and the successful sequence numbers are exactly those 13. Zel’s stream attempt counter only increases, so the fifth stream failure aborts even when each failure made progress.

An OK stream close with acknowledgements still missing is not retried and is a persistent `BES_STREAM_COMPLETED_WITH_UNACK_EVENTS_ERROR` with status `FAILED_PRECONDITION`. Zel returns the gRPC status string for the first two, and on OK with missing acks it resends until the retry cap and then returns `BES upload failed: not all events were acknowledged`.
  - An acknowledgement whose sequence is not the next expected one fails the upload immediately with transient `BES_UPLOAD_TIMEOUT_ERROR` and status `FAILED_PRECONDITION`, with no retry. Zel only moves the ack cursor forward, so a higher sequence marks the gap acknowledged and a lower sequence is ignored.

Zel’s `close` finishes with `Build Event Service upload timed out (--bes_timeout)`, and that same timeout also bounds the connector and lifecycle RPCs.
  - Local-file upload is absent. The tests require one upload per distinct path (duplicate paths collapse to one map entry), `named_set_of_files` URIs `cas://` plus the digest of the Latin-1 file bytes, and a failed second upload that is not retried: `close` fails transiently with `BES_UPLOAD_LOCAL_FILE_ERROR` whose cause is the `IOException` (`File upload failed.`), and the server stream error is `CANCELLED` or `INTERNAL`. Zel serializes the BEP event and does not upload referenced files.

### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/buildeventservice/BuildEventServiceTransportGrpcTest.java`
- Bazel lines: 192
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-events/src/bes.rs`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - Bazel serves a real plaintext gRPC endpoint on a free TCP port (`localhost:<port>`, no call credentials, no interceptor) and refuses to build the client unless that port is greater than 0 (`getPort()` is `-1` when the server is down). Zel’s fake BES is an in-memory HTTP/2 pair with authority `bes.local` and never binds a port.
  - With out-of-order acknowledgements enabled, Bazel ACKs `sequence_number + 1` and does not record the event as successful. The upload then fails once, with gRPC `FAILED_PRECONDITION`, exit `TRANSIENT_BUILD_EVENT_SERVICE_UPLOAD_ERROR`, and `BES_UPLOAD_TIMEOUT_ERROR`. Zel treats any ACK whose sequence is greater than `acked` as progress, so `sequence + 1` advances the cursor and can mark the stream fully acknowledged.
  - A null stream status still records the event and sends any buffered ACKs, but Bazel half-closes the RPC only when the status is non-null and OK. A predicate that always returns null therefore leaves the stream open and `close()` throws `TimeoutException`. Zel always finishes the tool stream with `grpc-status: 0`.
  - Bazel’s lifecycle default is OK only for sequence 1 on `BuildEnqueued` and `InvocationAttemptStarted`, and sequence 2 on `InvocationAttemptFinished` and `BuildFinished`; every other lifecycle event is `UNKNOWN`. The tool stream is completed only for `COMPONENT_STREAM_FINISHED`. Zel accepts every lifecycle call with status 0 and ends the tool stream after the messages in that call.
  - Injected `INVALID_ARGUMENT` on the tool stream is not retried and exits `PERSISTENT_BUILD_EVENT_SERVICE_UPLOAD_ERROR` / `BES_STREAM_NOT_RETRYING_FAILURE`. Stream `FAILED_PRECONDITION` exits transient / `BES_UPLOAD_TIMEOUT_ERROR`. Lifecycle `FAILED_PRECONDITION` exits persistent / `BES_STREAM_NOT_RETRYING_FAILURE`. An OK trailers frame with ACKs still outstanding is not retried, exits persistent / `BES_STREAM_COMPLETED_WITH_UNACK_EVENTS_ERROR`, and the client status is `FAILED_PRECONDITION`. Zel retries only `UNKNOWN`, `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`, `ABORTED`, `INTERNAL`, `UNAVAILABLE`, and `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` (stream budget 4, then `"BES upload failed: not all events were acknowledged"`). An OK stream with missing ACKs is resent. Any BES close error becomes exit `TRANSIENT_BUILD_EVENT_SERVICE_UPLOAD_ERROR`; persistent exit 45 and those `BuildProgress` codes are not produced. A close deadline uses `"Build Event Service upload timed out (--bes_timeout)"`.
  - Bazel records every attempt in a per-`StreamId` insertion-order multimap, including failures, and a separate successful-event multimap. `UNAVAILABLE` lifecycle retries are stored twice per event, in order. Zel’s UNAVAILABLE case returns before appending, so the failed attempt is absent, and the test only checks that the later successful stream has at least five requests and exactly four lifecycle messages.
  - Bazel sets `publishBuildToolEventStreamAccepted` when the RPC is accepted, before any message. A client `onError` is stored via `Status.fromThrowable`. A failed local-file upload is expected to surface there as `CANCELLED` or `INTERNAL`, with exit transient / `BES_UPLOAD_LOCAL_FILE_ERROR` and cause `"File upload failed."`. Zel drops unexpected stream events and has no client-cancel status.
  - This harness fixes the VFS digest to SHA256. File-upload cases write bytes with Latin-1, publish `cas://` plus the SHA-256 of the UTF-8 strings `"file1"` and `"file2"`, and collapse duplicate paths to one upload. Zel’s BES tests do not upload local files or check digests.
  - Bazel can withhold ACKs until a later request (batch mode) and, if lifecycle handling throws, return `INTERNAL` with that exception’s message. Zel ACKs each tool-stream message immediately and has no lifecycle `INTERNAL` path.

### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/buildtool/EnvironmentRestrictedBuildTest.java`
- Bazel lines: 438
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - Analysis does not enforce `--target_environment`. A target with no `compatible_with` and no group default still builds when the flag names an environment; Bazel fails analysis with `//foo:bar declares compatibility with:` / `[]` / `but does not support:` / `//buildenv:one`.
  - Explicit `compatible_with` matching every repeated `--target_environment` is not required. Bazel fails a target compatible only with `//buildenv:one` when `//buildenv:two` is also requested, listing `[//buildenv:one]` and `//buildenv:two`.

  - A package wildcard such as `//foo:all` is not failed because one expanded target lacks the requested environment. Bazel names that target (`//foo:bad_bar`) and its declared set (`[//buildenv:two]`).

  - A missing environment label does not fail with `invalid target environment: no such target '//buildenv:nada'`.
  - A non-environment target does not fail with `//foo:bar is not a valid environment definition`.
  - `select()` does not refine supported environments. Bazel succeeds when `--define mode=one` keeps a dependency compatible with `//buildenv:one`, and fails when `--define mode=two` drops it, with `//foo:toplevel declares compatibility with:` / `[//buildenv:one, //buildenv:two]` / `environment: //buildenv:one` / `removed by: //foo:toplevel`.
  - Top-level output files and aliases do not inherit the generating rule's environments. Bazel accepts `//foo:libbar.a` and an alias to a compatible genrule output, and rejects an alias to an incompatible output on the output label `//foo:badgen.out` with declared compatibility `[]`.
  - Only environments named by the flag are required. Bazel still succeeds for `--target_environment=//buildenv/a:a1` when the target is `restricted_to` `//buildenv/b:b2` and does not declare group `a`.

### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/buildtool/GenQueryIntegrationTest.java`

  - There is no transitive scope closure. Missing scope targets or packages, missing transitive scope targets or packages, and unselected `select` branches do not fail the build. Bazel fails with `errors were encountered while computing transitive closure of the scope` plus `no such target '//b:target': target 'target' not declared in package 'b' defined by …/b/BUILD`, `no such package 'b': BUILD file not found in any of the following directories…`, `no such package 'dne': …`, and `Target '//d:d' contains an error and its package is in error`.
  - Streamed label output is reverse-postorder topological order, not the lexicographic order graphless genquery writes. Asserted orders differ, including `//a:z` before `//fruits:melon`, `//spices:in*` before `//spices:top`, the aspect-chain labels, and `//foo:BUILD` before `//foo:bzl.bzl`. Top-level `somepath` is reordered the same way. Bazel keeps path order.
  - Query failures omit the `query failed:` text the tests assert. A missing target is `in genquery rule //a:query: no such target '//b:nosuchtarget': …`, and the loadfiles/buildfiles location failure omits `query failed:` before `Query expressions involving 'buildfiles' or 'loadfiles' cannot be used with --output=location`.

  - `--nograph:factored` is unrecognized, so the unfactored graph build fails. Bazel prints one edge from `//fruits:melon` to each of coconut, mango, and papaya. The default factored graph is produced.
  - `--consistent_labels` is unrecognized, so the build fails instead of printing `@@//fruits:melon` and `@@//fruits:papaya`.
  - `compressed_output = True` is ignored. The output is plain label text stored with `String::from_utf8_lossy`, not gzip bytes that decompress to `//fruits:melon\n//fruits:papaya\n`.
  - Editing a package reached only through the scope's dependencies does not invalidate the genquery. Analysis depends on the genquery's own package, and `scope` labels are not configured, so a later `:coconut` dep does not show up. Bazel recomputes and includes it.

With `--experimental_frontier_violation_check=warn`, the same change emits that text, `will be discarding the analysis cache`, and `Focusing on`, and keeps the previous active set for both derived and explicit sets.
  - An explicit file rebuilds when that file changes (`x\ny` to `x2\ny`). An explicit directory rebuilds source edits and `BUILD` reanalysis (new target output `y`). A parent directory also rebuilds a child-package source (`x2\ny` to `x2\ny2`). Targets that were not the original focus, including one with no sources, can still be built.
  - A package error fails target parsing with `Package 'hello' contains errors`, leaves Skyfocus enabled, and leaves the verification set empty.

Widening the flag to include that path then succeeds with the new contents.

The planted set in that test (`pkgA`, `dir1/pkgA`, `dir1/pkgB`, `dir2/pkg/file`, `dir2/pkg/pkg`, `pkgB/file`, `pkgB/dir/file`, `pkgB/dir/pkg`, `pkgB/pkg`) is not produced.

The prefix check uses lossy UTF-8 (`to_string_lossy`) rather than the filesystem basename as a Java string (Unix Latin-1 bytes): a non-UTF-8 name whose bytes start with the prefix is deleted. An unreadable directory is not made readable and retried; removal fails with the OS error.

### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/concurrent/CancellableTaskTest.java`
- Bazel lines: 658

  - Zel has no `CancellableTask`. `runIfNotCancelled` may run the body only once and returns true; a second call throws `IllegalStateException`. Cancel before start (`cancelAndAwait`, or `requestCancellation` then `awaitCompletion`) makes `runIfNotCancelled` return false and skips the body. A second cancel before or after a finished run returns without blocking.
  - Cancel during the body interrupts it and does not return until the body finishes. `requestCancellation` alone interrupts and returns while the body is still running. A later `awaitCompletion` waits without a second interrupt, so post-interrupt cleanup is not aborted. If `cancelAndAwait` is interrupted while waiting, it throws `InterruptedException`; a retry interrupts the still-running body again and waits until it finishes.
  - The optional completion action runs once, after the body, including when the body throws `IOException` with message `"task failed"` (that exception still propagates). Cancel before start also runs completion once; a repeated cancel or a prevented run does not run it again. A second canceller, and a `runIfNotCancelled` that loses the claim, both wait until that completion finishes; the losing run returns false. Cancellation during completion waits for it and does not interrupt it.
  - Cancel from the body or from completion throws `IllegalStateException`. `runIfNotCancelled` from the cancel-before-start completion throws `IllegalStateException`. Completion throwing `IllegalStateException` with message `"completion failed"` propagates from `runIfNotCancelled` or from the cancel call, then still marks the task terminal: a later cancel returns, and `runIfNotCancelled` returns false.
  - `runIfNotCancelled` on an already cancelled task returns false and restores the caller’s interrupt status (`Thread.interrupted()` stays true). With one runner and two `cancelAndAwait` callers, exactly one claim wins: the body runs at most once, completion runs exactly once, and `runIfNotCancelled` is true only when the body ran. A normal return from cancel means the body is not running and completion has finished.

Zel writes only `total_time` (`seconds = ms/1000`, `nanos = (ms%1000)*1000000`), including when `total_time_ms` is 0, and only if `include_spawn_metrics` is set (default on unless `--experimental_execution_log_spawn_metrics` is `false`, `0`, or `no`). With no catastrophe, a `DetailedException` wins over an undetailed error and over a cycle: message contains `failed: bork`, failure detail is that exception's `Query.Code.BUILD_FILE_ERROR` (exit code 7), and no bug report is sent. Results may be inaccurate`.

An error with `keepGoing` false, or `keepGoing` true plus a catastrophe (`catas`), runs a second `evaluate` on an empty key list. `keepGoing` true with an undetailed error and no catastrophe, and a cycle-only error, return with no second evaluation and no bug report. Zel has no empty re-evaluation and no cycle-only preload success path.

Bazel parses each expression with `QueryExpression.parse` and returns a `long` that sums AST text lengths only: target-literal patterns (including `$var` references), function `WORD` arguments, and `let` variable names. Function names, operators, parentheses, and the `let`/`in` keywords add nothing. An `INTEGER` argument would add `1`. These weights are asserted and have no zel counterpart: `"$x - attr('tags', 'foo', $x)"` is `11`; `"kind('pat', allrdeps(//a + //b + //c + //d + //e + //f))"` is `21`; `"let x = (let x = //... in $x - deps($x)) in $x - allrdeps($x)"` is `15`; `"let x = $x in $x - allrdeps($x)"` is `7`; `"let x = (let y = //... in $x - deps($y)) in $x - allrdeps($y)"` is `15`; `"$x + set($x)"` is `4`.
  - Rebinding does not change the sum and does not fail: the same-variable and different-variable nested `let`s both weigh `15`, and `let x = $x` still counts the `$x` pattern (`2`) plus the name `x` (`1`). `set($x)` weighs the word `$x` (`2`), the same as a bare target literal, so the `set` wrapper adds `0`.

### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/remote/ChunkedBlobUploaderTest.java`
- Bazel lines: 514
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - Zel has no chunked blob uploader. `getChunkingThreshold()` for `FastCdcChunkingConfig(512, 2, 0)` returns `512 * 4` (`2048`). The default uploader under test uses `FastCdcChunkingConfig(1024, 2, 0)` and SHA-256.
  - `uploadChunked` queries missing digests, uploads every missing chunk, and the sum of chunk sizes equals the file length. An 8192-byte file (random seed 42) yields more than one chunk.
  - `force=true` is forwarded as the boolean argument on every chunk `uploadBlob` call, once per digest returned by the missing-digest query. `force=false` is the other path.
  - When the missing-digest set is empty, no chunk `uploadBlob` runs, and `spliceBlob` is still called with the original blob digest.
  - When only some chunks are missing (first, last, and odd indexes), only those chunks are uploaded and their bytes must match the file slices. `spliceBlob` receives the full ordered chunk-digest list, including chunks that were already present.
  - At most 16 chunk uploads are in flight. With 17 distinct missing chunks, the 17th `uploadBlob` is not started until one in-flight upload completes (the test completes index 1). After the window drains, `spliceBlob` is called with the full chunk-digest list, including duplicate digests, not only the unique set. Waits are 1s for the first window, 100ms to confirm the overflow upload has not started, 1s for the overflow upload, and 1s for the upload thread to exit.
  - If one in-flight chunk fails with `IOException` message `"upload failed"`, the other in-flight upload futures are cancelled (`isCancelled() == true`) and `spliceBlob` is not called.
  - An already-cancelled chunk upload future makes `uploadChunked` throw `InterruptedException` and skip `spliceBlob`.
  - If the first chunk upload is already failed with `IOException` `"upload failed"` while later chunks are still pending, the failure is surfaced before a second `getInputStream()` (`getInputStream` is called exactly once) and `spliceBlob` is not called.
  - If the file is truncated before the missing chunk is read (second `getInputStream()` returns an empty stream), `uploadChunked` throws `IOException` whose message contains `"file was concurrently modified during upload"` and whose cause is `EOFException`. `spliceBlob` is not called.

### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/remote/ReaderPreferringReadWriteLockTest.java`
- Bazel lines: 357
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - Ten shared readers may all hold the lock at once. After every reader unlocks, a writer can lock and unlock.
  - Unlocking a read or write lock that the caller does not hold throws `IllegalMonitorStateException`. Unlocking the other mode while one mode is held also throws `IllegalMonitorStateException`.
  - A reader blocks while a writer holds the lock, and a writer blocks while a reader holds it. The waiter acquires exactly once after release, and the original mode can lock again.
  - A second writer blocks until the first writer unlocks, then acquires exactly once.
  - While a writer waits on an existing reader, another reader is still admitted. The writer acquires only after every reader unlocks, then both modes can lock again.
  - If a new reader locks after the last reader drops the count but before the writer is woken, the writer waits again and is not stranded. It acquires only after that new reader unlocks.
  - A blocked reader or writer interrupted while waiting throws `InterruptedException` and does not take the lock. The holder still owns it, and after unlock both modes can lock.
  - Interrupting the only writer waiting on a reader leaves later readers off the intrinsic monitor: three read lock/unlock cycles must not enter `BLOCKED` while another thread holds `synchronized` on the lock.
  - A thread already interrupted before `lockReadInterruptibly` or `lockWriteInterruptibly` throws `InterruptedException` and does not take the lock. The other mode can then lock and unlock. The interrupt status is cleared afterward.
  - Sixteen threads, each seeded `Random(0)` through `Random(15)` and running 20,000 iterations, take a write with probability 1/4 and a read otherwise. A writer must observe exactly one writer and zero readers. A reader must observe zero writers. Any `InterruptedException` is a violation. After all threads finish, violations, readers, and writers are all 0.

### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/remote/RemoteRetrierTest.java`
- Bazel lines: 172
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-remote/src/grpc.rs`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - Jittered backoff (`initial` 1s, `max` 10s, multiplier 2, jitter 0.1, 6 attempts) must land in `[900,1100)`, `[1800,2200)`, `[3600,4400)`, `[7200,8800)`, `[9000,11000)`, `[9000,11000)` ms, then stop. Bazel uses `jitter * (ThreadLocalRandom.nextDouble(2.0) - 1)` so the factor is `[1-jitter, 1+jitter)`, then truncates to a `long` millisecond. Zel uses `r = (subsec_nanos % 2001) / 1000.0 - 1.0` (`[-1, 1]` inclusive, 2001 clock steps), so the factor is `[1-jitter, 1+jitter]` and those delays can be exactly 1100, 2200, 4400, 8800, or 11000 ms. Both jitter the already capped base, so the 5th and 6th bases are 10000 ms and the jittered sleep may exceed 10s.
  - Zero-jitter bases 1000, 2000, 4000, 8000, 10000, 10000 ms match `min(initial * multiplier^attempt, max)`. Bazel then stores `(long)(nextDelayMillis * multiplier)`, so a non-integral step diverges: initial 3 ms and multiplier 1.5 yield 3, 4, 6, 9, 13 ms, while Zel keeps `f64` seconds (3, 4.5, 6.75, 10.125, 15.1875 ms) and rounds only in `Duration::from_secs_f64`. Per-call reset matches: maxAttempts 2 sleeps 1000 then 2000 and invokes the call 3 times; two executes sleep 1000 twice, 2000 twice, and invoke it 6 times. Zel stops when `attempt >= max_retries` instead of returning a negative delay.
  - `testNonRetriableError` forces `PERMANENT_FAILURE` for `Status.Code.UNKNOWN` and expects one call and a thrown `StatusRuntimeException` even with 2 attempts. Zel `RetryPolicy::is_retriable` always retries `UNKNOWN`, `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`, `ABORTED`, `INTERNAL`, `UNAVAILABLE`, and `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`, and `run` takes no classifier, so `max_retries = 2` invokes the call 3 times.
  - `InterruptedException` is not classified and not retried; the same instance is rethrown (`isSameInstanceAs`) even when the classifier returns `TRANSIENT_FAILURE`. Zel `run` only returns `Result<T, GrpcStatus>` and `std::thread::sleep` does not observe an interrupt or pass through a separate interruption error.
  - `ReapiClient::execute` in `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-remote/src/reapi_client.rs` does not use `RetryPolicy::delay`. It sleeps `Duration::from_millis(10 * attempt)` (10 ms, then 20 ms, …). A `NOT_FOUND` status while an operation name is set clears the name and retries without checking `max_retries`, so `--remote_retries=0` still retries that case.

The runfiles action itself is not excluded. An unrelated producer and the runfiles action finish within 10000 ms while the tree's producer stays blocked until the closeable is released.

The lock order that must complete within 10000 ms is: consumer holds its output write lock, downstream expanded action holds the upstream file read lock and blocks on the consumer, upstream producer blocks on that read lock, then the consumer still acquires the upstream tree read lock and all three finish.
