### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/remote/RetrierTest.java`
- Bazel lines: 454
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-remote/src/grpc.rs`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - No circuit breaker. With `ZeroBackoff(3)` and a breaker that trips after 2 consecutive failures, Bazel stops and throws `CircuitBreakerException` (not `"call failed"`), leaves `consecutiveFailures == 2` and state `REJECT_CALLS`, and does not consume the remaining retries. `TRIAL_CALL` runs once: success returns `10` and moves to `ACCEPT_CALLS`; failure is not retried and `consecutiveFailures` becomes `1`. `REJECT_CALLS` rejects before the callable runs.
  - An interrupted thread throws `InterruptedException` (null message) and does not invoke the callable (`numCalls == 0`). A thrown `InterruptedException` is not retried (`numCalls == 1`) and is not classified, so neither `recordFailure` nor `recordSuccess` runs. `RetryPolicy::run` does not check interruption.
  - `EXPERIMENTAL_GRPC_RESULT_CLASSIFIER`: `ABORTED`, `UNKNOWN`, and `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` are each tried 3 times (`ZeroBackoff(2)`) and every attempt increments consecutive failures (total 9, then `REJECT_CALLS`). `PERMISSION_DENIED`, `UNIMPLEMENTED`, `DATA_LOSS`, and `OUT_OF_RANGE` are tried once each and each increments consecutive failures until `REJECT_CALLS`. `NOT_FOUND` and `ALREADY_EXISTS` are not retried but count as success: `consecutiveFailures` resets to `0` and state becomes `ACCEPT_CALLS`, while the status exception still fails the call (`ExecutionException` on the async path). Zel retries the first three and does not retry the others, with no success-versus-permanent split and no breaker. `RemoteClient::execute` also retries `NOT_FOUND` after an operation name is known by clearing that name and calling `Execute` again.
  - A classifier that marks every error success performs one call, rethrows message `"call failed"`, calls `recordSuccess` once, and never `recordFailure`. Exhausted retries (`maxRetries=2`) perform 3 calls, rethrow `"call failed"`, call `recordFailure` 3 times, and never `recordSuccess`. Success on the third call returns `1`, with 2 `recordFailure` calls and 1 `recordSuccess`. Zel returns the last `GrpcStatus` (unit-test message `"x"`) after `max_retries + 1` attempts and has no breaker callbacks.
  - Async failures fail the future with `ExecutionException` whose cause message is `"call failed"` or `""` (`new Exception("")`). Zel returns `Err(GrpcStatus)` from synchronous `run` and does not wrap a cause whose message is empty.

  - With `checkActionResultIntegrity` true, Bazel refreshes output-file digests, then each directory's tree blob, `Tree.root`, and every `Tree.children` directory's files, then stdout, then stderr, and stops at the first missing digest. The test tree leaves `root` unset and puts the file only on `children`, and that file is required. Zel checks output files, then stdout, then stderr, then directories through `flatten_tree`, which returns `"tree has no root"` when `root` is unset and only walks children linked from the root by digest. That test tree is a miss even when the file blob is present, and that file's mtime is not updated. With the flag false, Bazel still returns the `ActionResult` (exit code left unchanged) and refreshes mtimes of blobs that exist, including those after the missing one. Zel returns the result and refreshes only the AC file.
  - Bazel updates the AC mtime before reading it, including when the result is later discarded as stale (`null`), and refreshes referenced blobs after that so the blobs are newer than the action result. Zel updates the AC mtime only after integrity succeeds, so a stale lookup leaves the seeded mtime `0` in place, and blob mtimes are updated before the AC mtime.
  - `uploadFile`, `uploadBlob`, and `uploadActionResult` `fsync` the temp file before rename. Zel writes or copies and renames without a sync. CAS still keeps existing bytes and only refreshes mtime; an AC upload still replaces the bytes (exit code 42, then 43). `uploadFile` still forces mode `0644` and does not keep the source mtime.

### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/remote/disk/DiskCacheGarbageCollectorTest.java`
- Bazel lines: 257
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - Zel has no disk-cache garbage collector. `DiskCache` only stores, reads, and refreshes entry mtimes. `--experimental_disk_cache_gc_max_size` and `--experimental_disk_cache_gc_max_age` are parsed and never applied.
  - No size policy. Bazel keeps the cache at or under the max size (these cases use 1024-byte KiB units) by deleting oldest entries first. Equal mtimes break ties by path ascending, so `ac/123` and `ac/abc` are deleted before `cas/456` and `cas/def`.
  - No age policy. An entry whose age is greater than or equal to the max age is deleted (a file exactly 3 days old is deleted when the max age is 3 days). Newer entries stay.
  - No combined policy. Bazel applies the more restrictive of size and age. When both limits are already satisfied, nothing is deleted. Expected stats are total entries, total bytes, deleted entries, deleted bytes, `concurrentUpdate=false`, and `Duration.ZERO`.
  - Files under `gc/` and `tmp/` are neither counted nor deleted. With only those files, max size `1`, and max age 1 day, stats stay `(0, 0, 0, 0, false, Duration.ZERO)`.
  - If a shared lock is already held on `<root>/gc/lock`, collection fails with an `IOException` whose message contains `failed to acquire exclusive filesystem lock`. Zel takes no such lock.

### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/remote/grpc/DynamicConnectionPoolTest.java`

  - With `maxConcurrencyPerConnection` 1, two subscribed `create()` calls both complete: the first underlying connection is `connection0`, the second is `connection1`, and `connectionFactory.create` runs twice. `Channel::pick_conn` reuses the least-loaded connection while `active_streams() < STREAMS_PER_CONN` (`100`). Two checkouts that have not opened 100 local streams share that connection, and `connector.connect` runs once. Another connection is opened only when every pooled connection already has at least 100 active streams and `conns.len() < max_connections` (`max_connections.max(1)`).

A `connect` that never returns leaves the second caller waiting on the same mutex.

Zel frees capacity when the HTTP/2 stream’s `active_local` count drops. `Conn::close` sends GOAWAY and `fail("connection closed locally")`; `pick_conn` then drops connections for which `is_closed()` is true and dials again.

Dial failures are gRPC status `UNAVAILABLE` with `"connection failed: {e}"` or `"h2 handshake failed: {e}"`.
  - `close()` during a pending create disposes the factory subscription (`canceled` becomes true), interrupts the sleeper so `finished` stays false, and fails the subscriber with `IllegalStateException` whose message contains `"closed"`. `Channel::close` takes the same mutex, so it runs after `connect` returns; that `pick_conn` already returned `Ok(conn)`. `Conn::close` then fails the connection with `io::Error` kind `ConnectionAborted` and message `"connection closed locally"`. `io_to_status` maps that to `UNAVAILABLE` and `"transport error: connection closed locally"`.

### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/remote/grpc/SharedConnectionFactoryTest.java`
- Bazel lines: 433
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - No zel type shares one underlying connection across a permit count. `SharedConnectionFactory(factory, maxConcurrency)` starts with `numAvailableConnections() == maxConcurrency` (`1` or `2`). A subscribed `create()` calls `ConnectionFactory.create()` once and returns that same connection; the count drops by one per holder. A second `create()` with no permit stays empty (no value, no error, no completion) until a holder `close()`s, then receives the same connection and the count stays `0`. With `maxConcurrency == 2`, two holders share one connection and the count goes `1` then `0`. Ten concurrent subscribers still call `create()` once and all see that connection.

  - After `factory.close()`, `create()` errors with `IllegalStateException` whose message contains `"closed"`. If creation is still in flight, close cancels it (`canceled == true`, `finished == false`) and the pending subscriber gets that same `IllegalStateException` (`"closed"`).
  - A fatal call status (`FatalIOException`, message `"fatal"`, on a `CLIENT_STREAMING` call named `"testMethod"` with `CallOptions.DEFAULT`) drops the shared connection. The next `create()` is a new connection; with `maxConcurrency == 2` the available count is `1` afterward.

  - Disposing the subscriber while creation is in flight leaves the factory `Single` uncanceled (`canceled == false`, `finished == true`) and returns the permit to `1`. Interrupting a thread blocked in `observer.await()` ends that waiter (`interrupted == true`) while the in-flight create stays unfinished (`finished == false`).
  - Zel `Channel` (`/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-remote/src/grpc.rs`) is a separate pool: `max_connections.max(1)`, another connection when every live conn has `active_streams() >= 100`, connect failure is `GrpcStatus` `UNAVAILABLE` with `"connection failed: {e}"` or `"h2 handshake failed: {e}"`. `Channel::close` GOAWAYs current conns with `"connection closed locally"` and the next `call` dials again.

### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/remote/grpc/TokenBucketTest.java`

- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - No zel type deduplicates in-flight and finished async tasks. `executeIfNot` does not subscribe until observed: an unsubscribed task does not run, and both in-progress and finished sets stay empty.
  - A successful result is delivered to the subscriber, the key leaves in-progress, and it is recorded in finished. An error is the same `Throwable` (tests use `IllegalStateException("error")`); the key is in neither set.
  - A second subscriber of an in-progress task shares the single execution and both receive `"value1"`. `execute(key, task, force=true)` while that key is in progress also does not start a second execution.
  - After the key is finished, `executeIfNot` returns the cached value with execution count 1. `execute(..., force=true)` starts a new execution: the new subscriber stays empty, execution count is 2, the key is in-progress again, and finished is empty.
  - Disposing the only subscriber runs the upstream cancellable, and the key is in neither set. Disposing one of two subscribers does not cancel and leaves the key in-progress. Disposing both cancels and clears both sets.
  - Completing one of two keys emits only that value; the other key stays in-progress and unfinished.
  - `AsyncTaskCache.NoResult.execute(key, task, force=true)` is stressed with 1000 tasks, keys `"key" + random.nextInt(20)`, a pool of 1000 threads, and upstream sleep of `0..999` ms. One loop mixes `dispose()` with `await()` and requires `assertNoErrors()`. The other converts the task to a `Future` and either `cancel(true)` or `get()`. Any `Throwable` other than `InterruptedException` fails the test; `InterruptedException` is swallowed after restoring the interrupt flag.
  - `shutdown()` with a still-running task sets shutdown and not terminated. A later `executeIfNot` fails with `CancellationException`. The same error is returned after `shutdown()` plus `awaitTermination()`.
  - `shutdown()` then `shutdownNow()` then `awaitTermination()` cancels the in-progress subscriber with `CancellationException` and leaves both shutdown and terminated true.
  - `awaitTermination()` after `shutdown()` blocks until the in-progress task succeeds, then both flags are true, the subscriber gets the value, and both in-progress and finished are empty. A second `awaitTermination()` after `shutdownNow()` and a first await returns immediately with both flags true.

### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/remote/util/FreePortFinder.java`
- Bazel lines: 68
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - `pickUnusedRandomPort` draws an unseeded `java.util.Random` port as `nextInt(64551) + 1024` (1024..=65574) and tries at most 128 times.
  - A port is usable only if a wildcard TCP `ServerSocket(port)` binds and then a wildcard UDP `DatagramSocket(port)` binds. Each socket calls `setReuseAddress(true)` after bind and is closed before the port is returned, so the port is not held. Ports `< 1024` or `> 65535` return unavailable, so 65536..=65574 always fail. If all 128 probes fail and the thread is not interrupted, it throws `IOException` with message `"Failed to find available port"`. A successful pick returns the `int` port and does not check interruption.

With `objc_generate_linkmap` the linkmap is `{package}/{name}.linkmap`. The objlist is `{package}/{name}-linker.objlist` in `multiline` format. Framework dedup keys are the second character of `-framework` or `-weak_framework` (`f` or `w`) plus the name; `-Wl,-framework,NAME` and `-Wl,-weak_framework,NAME` are rewritten to that two-arg form; `-Wl,-rpath,` is kept whole; `-l` flags are deduped by the whole flag; every other flag is repeated; a final `-framework` or `-weak_framework` with no following name is dropped. The default `strip` is `sometimes` and the default of `objc_enable_binary_stripping` is false. With stripping enabled, `opt` is true in Bazel and false in Zel, and `fastbuild` is false in Bazel and true in Zel, which changes the dSYM suffix above.

Bazel still returns the `experimental_objc_fastbuild_options` default `-O0`, `-DDEBUG=1` for `fastbuild` even when hardcoded flags are avoided (default of that flag is true). Zel never reads `objc_debug_with_GLIBCXX`. `checkClangCoptsForDebugModeWithoutGlib` requires `-DOS_IOS` in order and rejects `-D_GLIBCXX_DEBUG` when that flag is false.

Archive actions are the generator of `lib{name}.a`. Link actions are the generator of `{name}_bin`, or, when that is null, the generator of the `{name}_lipobin` input whose path ends in `_bin`. `requires-darwin` is required as an execution-info key. `APPLE_SDK_PLATFORM` and `XCODE_VERSION_OVERRIDE` must be entries of the action's incomplete environment. A `-filelist` param file's args must be exactly the exec paths of the named input suffixes, with no extras.

It hardcodes `/bin/bash`, ignores `--shell_executable`, and never emits `shExecutable must be non-null`.
  - Linux `--script_path` text is `#!/<shExecutable>`, then `cd <ShellEscaper(workingDir)> && \`, `exec env \`, sorted `-u UNSET_ME` / `-u UNSET_ME_TOO`, then sorted `ENV_VAR=val` / `ENV_VAR_WITH_SPACES='foo bar'`, then the escaped command and `"$@"` with no trailing newline. Zel’s script is always `#!/bin/bash`, quotes `cd` the same way for safe characters, and emits sorted `-u` / `KEY=value` lines, but the clear list also includes `JAVA_RUNFILES`, `RUNFILES_DIR`, `RUNFILES_MANIFEST_FILE`, `RUNFILES_MANIFEST_ONLY`, and `TEST_SRCDIR`, keys are not shell-escaped, the command is the absolute executable (or `external/bazel_tools/tools/test/test-setup.sh ./<name>` for a test) with no baked-in `argv1` / `'arg w spaces'`, and a run-under prefix is omitted from the script.

Zel `move_outputs` always writes `exec_root/<output>` (one path, no separate outputs root): skip if missing, `remove_dir_all` or `remove_file`, `create_dir_all` the parent, `rename`, else `copy_tree` (`read_link` for a symlink, recurse for a directory, `std::fs::copy` otherwise) with no `0644` retry, no that warning, and no unsupported-type message.

### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/server/CommandManagerTest.java`
- Bazel lines: 189

  - Bazel command ids are `UUID.randomUUID()` strings (`UUID.fromString` accepts them), and two nested `createCommand()` calls get different ids. Zel ids are `{server_pid}-{n}` with `next_id` starting at `1`, so the first Run is `{pid}-1`, then `{pid}-2`.
  - `isEmpty()` is true only when every `RunningCommand` is closed. Two commands may be open together, and after the inner close `isEmpty()` stays false until the outer close. Zel’s `running` count likewise stays non-zero for every in-flight Run, including one blocked on the lock, but the second command does not run beside the holder: it waits, or with `block_for_lock` false it fails with stderr `"Another command ({other}) is running. Exiting immediately.\n"` (`{other}` is `client_description`, or `"unknown"`). The wait text is `"Another command ({other}) is running. Waiting for it to complete on the server (server_pid={pid})...\n"`.
  - `waitForChange()` wakes on every register and every close, so two nested commands produce notification counts 1, 2, 3, then 4, including the create and the inner close that leave the map non-empty. Interrupting that waiter throws `InterruptedException` and ends the loop. Zel signals its condition variable when the exclusive lock is dropped and on Cancel. The idle loop polls `accept` every 20ms, and a lock waiter uses `wait_timeout` of 500ms plus a cancel flag.
  - With `doIdleServerTasks=true`, a command that registers an `IdleTask` named `"my idle task"` (default `delay()` `Duration.ZERO`) runs it as soon as that command’s close empties the map, before the next command. Starting the next command snapshots results in registration order and leaves them stored if that command never calls `getIdleTaskResults()`. The command after that sees exactly one result, name `"my idle task"`, status `SUCCESS`, and that call clears the list, so the following command gets null. A command that registers no tasks does not start an idle period and does not drop unretrieved results. With `doIdleServerTasks=false`, `setIdleTasks` does not run the task and the next `getIdleTaskResults()` is null. Zel `--idle_server_tasks` defaults to `true` (help `"Run System.gc() when the server is idle"`). When it is on, Zel waits until `running == 0` and `last_activity` has elapsed at least 10s, then once calls `save_to_disk` on the action cache. It keeps no name, status, or duration and does not hand a result to the next command. `idle_tasks_done` is set back to false when `last_activity` has elapsed under 1s. `--idle_server_tasks=false` skips that save.

- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-packages/src/resolve.rs`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - Zel has no `CollectPackagesUnderDirectory` value. `find_packages_below` / `walk_dirs` returns only directories that contain a `BUILD` file. It does not report `isDirectoryPackage`, and it does not record immediate children that are empty as false (`a1/b2`, `a2/b1/c2`) or non-package parents (`a1`, `a2/b1`) with a true/false child map.
  - With the default `--show_loading_progress=true`, Bazel emits progress `Loading package: a1/b1`, `Loading package: a2/b2`, `Loading package: a1/b1/c1`, `Loading package: a2/b1/c1`, and `Loading package: a2/b2/c1`. Zel never prints `Loading package:` (`show_loading_progress` is unused). The Starlark text `a1/b1/BUILD:1:1: name 'xxx' is not defined` and `a2/b2/BUILD:1:1: name 'yyy' is not defined` still matches.
  - The test evaluates with keep-going, so a `BUILD` of `xxx` / `yyy` still counts the directory as containing a package or error and the value succeeds. Zel `//...` (`TargetsBelowDirectory`) still loads those packages, then returns `error loading package 'a1/b1': Package 'a1/b1' contains errors` (first failure only) and drops the collected targets. Children are walked in sorted basename order, so `a1` is reported before `a2`.
  - Bazel follows the directory symlink `a2` → `a1` and loads both `Loading package: a1/b1/c1` and `Loading package: a2/b1/c1` (`a2` is true). Zel treats a directory symlink as a cycle when the followed directory's `node_id` is already in the ancestor list. `LocalFileSystem` always uses `node_id` 0 and `InMemoryFileSystem` uses `node_id` 2 for every directory, so `a2` is skipped and its package is not loaded, with no event.
  - A self-symlink yields `Failed to get information about path, for a1/circular, skipping: Symlink cycle` and the same for `a2/circular`. Zel `stat` fails (`too many levels of symbolic links` on the in-memory filesystem) and `walk_dirs` continues with no message.
  - A file named `DONT_FOLLOW_SYMLINKS_WHEN_TRAVERSING_THIS_DIRECTORY_VIA_A_RECURSIVE_TARGET_PATTERN` makes Bazel not follow `a3/dirlink`, so `a3` is false and `Loading package: a3/b1/c1` is absent. Zel does not look for that name. With distinct node ids, `a3/dirlink` would be entered and `a3/dirlink/b1/c1` loaded.
  - Excluded paths `a1`, `a2/b1`, and `a2/b2/c2` are omitted from the map (root entries are only `tools` true and `a2` true) and are not loaded: no `Loading package: a1/b1/c1`, `Loading package: a1/b1/c2`, `Loading package: a1/b2/c1`, `Loading package: a2/b1/c1`, `Loading package: a2/b1/c2`, or `Loading package: a2/b2/c2`, but `Loading package: a2/b2/c1` is loaded. Zel's walk has no excluded-path set. `.bazelignore`, `REPO.bazel`, and `--deleted_packages` skip whole directories, but a negative pattern subtracts targets only after `//...` has already walked and loaded them.

- Differences:

  - Same fingerprint and no links must compare equal; different fingerprints must compare unequal.
  - Matching self-cycles must compare equal: a node already seen on both sides is equal, and a visit-new mismatch is unequal.

  - The same shape with two distinct `d` nodes that share a fingerprint must compare unequal, because sharing is by node identity, not by fingerprint.

  - Two input directories are zipped in child order. Pairs `(f1,f4)`, `(f2,f5)`, and `(f3,f6)` become `input_dir1_f1_input_dir2_f4.out` and the two siblings, each containing both seed digits. One input of four files splits even indices into `target_output_dir1` (`f1`, `f3`) and odd indices into `target_output_dir2` (`f2`, `f4`).
  - An output tree of one `map_directory` is a valid input directory of a later one. The second tree's names are `input_dir1_f1.out_input_dir2_f4.out` and its siblings, and each file contains the first seed, `some data`, and the second seed. A second build of `//test:target` still materializes that chained tree.
  - `execution_requirements = {"local": "1"}` is on the execution info of every expanded `SpawnAction`. `env = {"SOME_ENV": "ENV_VALUE"}` is on each action's fixed environment. A `resource_set` callable returning `{"cpu": 3, "memory": 768}` is what `buildResourceSet(OS.DARWIN, 2)` reports: memory 768, CPU 3, local-test count 0. Expanded actions are addressed by template action index 0, 1, and 2 in child order.
  - `additional_params` accepts an int (`1`), a bool (`True`), and a string (`"some string"`), and the mapping still writes the three seed files. A list, tuple, `File`, depset, dict, or set fails analysis with `Expected one of [bool, int, string]; but got <type> in additional_params['some_key']`. An empty `input_directories` or `output_directories` fails analysis with `actions.map_directory() requires at least one input.` or `... at least one output.`
  - `fail("This is a test failure.")` inside the implementation fails the build during execution, and the message is on stderr. `template_ctx.declare_file("child", directory=input_dir.directory)` fails execution with `Cannot declare file `child` in non-output directory File...test/target_input_dir`.
  - Two `declare_file("child")` calls in the same output directory fail execution with `ERROR: file 'test/target_output_dir/child' is generated by these conflicting actions:`. The conflict is execution-time, so the test skips the serialization check that would fail first. Using an input directory, its first child, the output tree, the tool executable, or a file written outside the template as `outputs`, with progress message `some conflicting action`, fails execution with `action 'some conflicting action' has conflicting output '...<path>' that is an output of another action, thus causing an action conflict.` The paths are `test/target_input_dir`, `test/target_input_dir/input_dir_f1`, `test/target_output_dir`, `test/tool`, and `test/some_file`.
  - Returning `1`, `True`, `[1]`, or `(1, 2)` fails execution with `actions.map_directory() implementation non_none_impl at ... may not return a non-None value (got <repr>)`, using Starlark repr. A nested `def` or a `lambda` fails analysis with `Error in map_directory: to avoid unintended retention of analysis data structures, the function (declared at .../test/rule_def.bzl:...) must be declared by a top-level def statement`.
  - Zel's `actions` object has no `map_directory` method (`'actions' value has no field or method 'map_directory'` in `crates/zel-analysis/src/starlark_rule_actions.rs`). There is no `template_ctx`, no execution-time per-child expansion, and no `ExpandedDirectory`. `experimental_allow_map_directory` defaults to true and is never read. `declare_directory` only sets `is_tree_artifact`. The analysis-time action-graph conflict string uses the full exec path and never sees template-expanded children.

Below 1024 the text is the decimal plus ` B`. Otherwise a US `0.0` format of `value/1024.0` is used after shifting the value down by 10 while it is at least `1<<20` and a larger unit remains. The unit list stops at `TiB`, so `1L<<50` stays on `TiB` and prints `1024.0`.

- Bazel lines: 149

- Differences:

It returns a positive opaque handle even when creation fails, and the last error is empty after success and is cleared once read. `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-ffi-bridge/src/native.rs` is Unix-only and records Windows as unimplemented. Its process helpers are pid, signal, nice, and rusage.
  - A stdin write of an `(offset, length)` slice returns the byte count, closing stdin lets the child finish, and stdout returns that slice. One hundred 3-byte writes come back in order. `"HELLO"` can be read as `"HE"` then `"LLO"`. Writing 3 bytes from offset 1 of `01234` reads back into the middle of an existing buffer as `a123e`.
  - A negative offset or length, an offset past the buffer, a length past the buffer, or `Integer.MAX_VALUE` on stdout, stderr, or stdin returns `-1` and does not consume pending stdout. A later in-bounds read still returns `oob`.
  - Stdout and stderr are independent pipes. Interleaved `out1`..`out4` and `err1`..`err4` stay in order when the other stream is drained first.
  - Bytes available on a live stdout are the unread count (`7`, then `4`). After the stream is closed the count is `0` and the stream error is empty. After the process has exited, available is still non-negative and the stream error is empty. A finished process yields `0` from stdout and stderr reads, and a stdin write returns `-1`.
  - `waitFor` with a negative timeout returns `0` once the process exits, and the exit code is `42`. A 5-second sleep makes `waitFor` of 1000 ms return `1`.
  - A missing executable sets a last error containing `The system cannot find the file specified.` and a stdout read returns `0`. An `argv0` longer than 260 characters is launched through the `\\?\` prefix (`cmd.exe /c exit 42`).
  - The environment block is UTF-16LE and must end in four zero bytes. `ONE=one\0TWO=twotwo\0\0` replaces the environment so the child prints `one` and `twotwo`. A block with no NUL, one trailing UTF-16 NUL, the encoding of `a`, or a single UTF-16 NUL is an error. Exactly `\0\0` succeeds. Zel never checks that layout. `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-sandbox/src/process_wrapper.rs` takes a string map.
  - Redirecting stdout and stderr to two files yields `one` and `two` after the wait, and the handle is greater than 0. The same path for both concatenates `onetwo`. Reads of those redirected streams return `0`. Merging stderr into stdout yields `onetwo` on stdout and `0` from stderr. Redirect opens for append, so existing `out1` and `err1` become `out1out2` and `err1err2`. The child working directory is the directory passed in, including a path written with `/`. `process_wrapper.rs` truncates a redirect with `set_len(0)` and spawns with `setsid` and `wait4`.

The returned list is the fixed-size `Arrays.asList` view, and a repeatable option flattens it with `putAll`. Zel’s comma-list converter (`convert_comma_list`) treats an empty input as `[]` and keeps trailing empties (`"a,"` is `["a", ""]`, `","` is `["", ""]`).

The enforcer is then built from `InvocationPolicyParser.parsePolicy` of that startup option’s `invocationPolicy` string, with log level `Level.INFO` and a null conversion context. An empty policy is empty bytes and an empty base64 value, and `parsePolicy` of a null or empty string returns the default policy. A base64 string that decodes but is not a valid `InvocationPolicy` fails as `OptionsParsingException` with the text `Malformed value of --invocation_policy: ` plus the original string, and that failure does not fall through to text format. Unknown flags are logged at INFO (`Flag '%s' specified by invocation policy does not exist, and will be ignored`), and value conversion and default lookup see a null context. Zel policy tests parse a text proto and call `apply_invocation_policy` directly. `InvocationPolicy::parse` still tries text format when base64 bytes are not a valid policy, and an unknown flag is skipped with no log.

A null name fails inside `ImmutableSet.of` instead of returning null (the enforcer’s null result message is `Command %s does not exist`). Zel `InvocationPolicy::applies_to_command` uses `get_command_ancestry`, which always starts with `always` and `common` and then walks inheritance (`test` is `always`, `common`, `build`, `test`). A policy named `build` therefore applies to `test`, and a policy named `always` or `common` applies even when the command is unknown. Zel has no per-suite hook that narrows ancestry to the command name alone.

### `src/test/java/com/google/devtools/common/options/ShellQuotedParamsFilePreProcessorTest.java`
- Bazel lines: 177
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - Zel never expands a sole `@params` argument by reading that file as UTF-8 and tokenizing it with shell single quotes. Option parsing has no params-file preprocessor, and worker `@file` expansion splits on lines without these quote rules.
  - Unquoted space and tab separate arguments, and a repeated separator yields an empty argument (`arg1 arg2 arg3\targ4\ arg5` → `arg1`, `arg2`, ``, `arg3`, `arg4\`, `arg5`). A backslash outside quotes is literal.

  - The four-character sequence `'\''` inside a quoted word is one embedded `'`, so `'ar'\''g1'` and `'a'\''rg'\''2'` become `ar'g1` and `a'rg'2`.
  - Quotes may open and close mid-word: `ar'g1 ar'g2 arg3` is `arg1 arg2` and `arg3`.
  - An unquoted `\'` does not escape the quote. `ar\'g1'` keeps the backslash and then enters a quote, producing `ar\g1`.
  - An unclosed quote fails with `Error reading params file: <path> Unfinished quote ' at <offset>`, where the offset is the quote's character index (`2` for `ar'g1`). Zel has no such error.

Zel does not require a conversion to equal itself, a second conversion from the same instance, and a conversion from another instance.

Zel does not reject unequal values inside one group or equal values placed in different groups.

### `src/test/java/net/starlark/java/annot/processor/StarlarkMethodProcessorTest.java`
- Bazel lines: 337

This suite runs `StarlarkMethodProcessor` on Java fixtures and requires either a clean compile or a specific compile error. Handwritten Rust binders and `.bzl` `def` parameter checks do not apply these rules.
  - `GoldenCase` must compile: a struct field with no parameters, an undocumented struct field that takes `StarlarkSemantics`, methods with named and mixed positional/named parameters (including defaults after required positionals, then named-only), `useStarlarkThread` as a trailing `StarlarkThread`, `extraKeywords` as a supertype of `Dict<String, Object>`, `extraPositionals` as a supertype of `Tuple` (`Sequence<?>`), wildcard generics `Sequence<?>` and `Dict<?, ?>`, and one non-empty `selfCall`.
  - Visibility and shape are rejected: a non-public method (`StarlarkMethod-annotated methods must be public.`), a static method (`StarlarkMethod-annotated methods cannot be static.`), an empty `name` (`StarlarkMethod.name must be non-empty.`), two methods with the same Starlark name (`Containing class defines more than one method named 'conflicting_method'`), and more than one `selfCall` (`Containing class has more than one selfCall method defined.`).
  - `structField=true` is rejected together with any `@Param` (`method structFieldMethod is annotated structField=true but also has 1 Param annotations`), `useStarlarkThread`, `extraPositionals`, `extraKeywords`, or `selfCall=true`.
  - Documentation is rejected when `documented` is true and `doc` is empty (`The 'doc' string must be non-empty if 'documented' is true.`), when a positional parameter is undocumented (`Parameter 'one' must be documented because it is positional`), and when any undocumented parameter is combined with `extraKeywords` (`Method 'undocumented_with_kwargs' has undocumented parameters but also allows extra keyword parameters`).
  - Parameter layout is rejected: more `@Param`s than Java parameters (`method methodWithParams has 1 Param annotations but only 0 parameters`); too few variables for special parameters (`method threeArgMethod is annotated with 1 Params plus 2 special parameters, but has only 2 parameter variables`); surplus variables (`method methodWithTooManyArguments is annotated with 1 Params plus 0 special parameters, yet has 2 parameter variables`); a parameter that is neither positional nor named; a required positional after a defaulted positional; a positional after a non-positional; a positional-only parameter after a named or undocumented parameter.
  - Special parameters are rejected on the wrong Java type: `useStarlarkThread` must be exactly `StarlarkThread` (including when that slot is declared before the ordinary parameters), and `extraKeywords` must be a type to which `Dict<String, Object>` can be assigned.
  - A concrete type argument is rejected (`parameter 'one' has generic type net.starlark.java.eval.Sequence<java.lang.String>`); only wildcards and `Object` are allowed.
  - Semantic flags are rejected when both `enableOnlyWithFlag` and `disableWithFlag` are set on the method or on a parameter, when `extraKeywords` is toggled by a flag (`The extraKeywords parameter may not be toggled by semantic flag`), and when a flag-gated parameter has no `defaultValue` (`Parameter 'two' may be disabled by semantic flag, thus defaultValue must be set`).

### `src/test/java/net/starlark/java/eval/DynamicTypeCheckTest.java`
- Bazel lines: 384
- Zel counterpart: `none`

There is no mode that accepts type syntax and checks it, and no flag that turns checking off while still parsing annotations.
  - With checking on, these must fail and do not: `int` is not a subtype of `float`; `str` is not `int`; `def f(a: int = 'abc')` fails at definition with `parameter 'a' has default value of type 'str', declares 'int'`; `return 'abc'` from `-> int` fails with `returns value of type 'str', declares 'int'`.
  - List, dict, and set annotations are ignored. Missing list invariance (`list[bool]` vs `list[int]`, `list[list[int]|list[bool]]`, `list[list[int|bool]]`, `list[int]` vs `list[None|int]`), dict key/value mismatches including nested `list[str|int]`, and `set[bool]` vs `set[int]`.

Missing Collection of list, dict keys, set, and tuple (covariant elements); Sequence of list and tuple but not dict or set; Mapping of dict with covariant values and invariant keys. The test binds those three names to `None` so the annotations resolve.

There is no union lattice: no dedup or associativity, and no `Any`/`Object` rules (`Any` is both a subtype and a supertype of `int|bool`; `Any|bool` is not a subtype of `int` while a union of only `Any` is; `Object` is not a subtype of `int|bool` but `int|bool` is a subtype of `Object`; `Any|Object` is not a subtype of `int` but is a subtype of `Any|int`).

The asserted forms are absent, including `hash: (str, /) -> int`, `int: (str|bool|int|float, /, base: [int]) -> int`, `range` to `Sequence[int]`, string methods such as `rsplit: (str, /, sep: str, maxsplit: [int]) -> list[str]`, and list methods typed as `Any` rather than the element type. Unannotated lambdas run, because no call is type-checked.

Leading spaces and indentation are stripped, a blank line or a plain `#` ends the block, a trailing `#:` overrides a leading one and applies only to the last statement on that line, and `#:` inside a string is not a doc comment. Both names are keywords, so `something.cast` and `(cast)(list, x)` are syntax errors. `type X = list` and `def f[T, U](...)` keep their type parameters (identifiers only, duplicates rejected, trailing comma allowed, `[]` rejected). A non-type annotation is `expected a type` unless `tolerateInvalidTypeExpressions` is set. Zel's `allow_type_syntax` skips `bazel_syntax` entirely. The execution parser then drops `x: T` and `type X = ...` as `Pass`, so the name is not declared, parses annotations as value expressions (`def f(a: (lambda x: x))` succeeds), treats `cast` and `isinstance` as ordinary calls, has no ellipsis token, and rejects `def f[T]()` because `[` is not `(`. With that flag on, the diagnostic parser no longer rejects chained comparisons, `;;`, implicit string concatenation, or `with` / `try` / `class` / `del`.

The execution parser's `if` clause calls `parse_or`, which does not accept `lambda`, so the same comprehension fails with `syntax error at 'lambda': expected expression`.
  - With `failFast` off, a file with errors still returns every statement that was recovered. `f(1, [x for foo foo foo foo], 3)` is a call of three arguments whose middle argument is an identifier whose name is the source text `[x for foo foo foo foo]`. `def foo` / `d = 4 ada` / `def bar` yields three statements and the three errors `syntax error at 'for'`, `syntax error at 'ada'`, and `syntax error at '*'`. The execution parser returns on the first error and builds no tree. `bazel_syntax` collects at most five parser errors and does not return that statement list.
  - Five thousand nested `{` characters are a syntax error whose message contains `internal error: stack overflow`, `parseDictEntry`, `Please report the bug`, and `foo.star` (the expression entry also quotes a prefix of the source). Neither Zel parser turns a deep recursion into that error.

Unary `-5` occupies `[0, 2)` and `- 5` occupies `[0, 3)`. `'abc' + 'def'` (either quote style) is one string literal `"abcdef"` covering `[0, 13)`, and repeated literals such as `"cat"` are interned to one instance. The execution AST stores a start line and column, literals use the default `0:0` location, and there is no end offset. `'abc' + 'def'` stays a `+` of two strings, and each literal is its own string.

Bazel rejects a second assignment, a second `def` of the same name, and a second `load` of the same local name with `'x' redeclared at top level` plus `'x' previously declared here`. Zel allows repeated assignments and repeated `def`s. A second `load` of the same local name fails inside `resolve_module` as `load statement defines 'x' more than once` (the intra-statement duplicate wording, with no previous-declaration note). `allowToplevelRebinding` does not exist, so duplicate loads stay illegal when that flag would allow them.

Zel never reports the conflict, so a load and an assignment of the same name are always accepted. A function that reads a load name is not recorded as a closure (Cell/Free); the name is looked up as a module global.
  - A load after another statement is only partly checked. Bazel (`requireLoadStatementsFirst`, the default) reports both `load statements must appear before any other statement` and `\tfirst non-load statement appears here`. Zel reports only the first message, and only when `allow_late_loads` is false. `eval_file_checked` sets that from the filename (`.bzl` forbids late loads; any other name allows them), not from `FileOptions`.
  - Top-level `if` and `for` are resolver errors in Bazel for every file (`if statements are not allowed at the top level…`, `for loops are not allowed at the top level…`). `resolve_module` accepts both. Zel emits those messages only from `eval_file_checked` in `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-starlark/src/lib.rs` when `static_names` is set and the file name ends in `.bzl`.
  - `name '…' is not defined` (other functions’ locals and parameters, `[foo for x in []]`, `lambda: undef`, and the same forward-reference rules the tests accept) is not reported by `resolver.rs`. `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-starlark/src/syntax/checks.rs` (`check_undefined_names`) does match those rules, but only when `strict_names` or `static_names` is on. Otherwise evaluation turns the identifier into a rule callable.
  - No identifier gets a scope or index (Local, Global, Cell, Free, Predeclared, Universal). A global assignment does not shadow a predeclared of the same name for the whole file, so `pre` before `pre = 1` still reads the predeclared value. Comprehension loop variables are written into the enclosing function’s locals for the duration of the comprehension. A name assigned anywhere in a nested function is not local to that whole function: a read before the assignment still sees the enclosing binding.
  - `#:` doc comments are dropped. There is no `docCommentsMap`, so a leading comment, a trailing comment shared by every name of a list assignment, and comments on annotated assignments are not associated with those names.
  - Non-lvalue assignment does not quote the target. Bazel reports `cannot assign to '"a"'`. Zel’s parser reports `cannot assign to non-lvalue expression` (`/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-starlark/src/syntax/parser.rs`). `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-starlark/src/syntax/bazel_syntax.rs` does not diagnose this case.
  - Experimental type syntax is not resolved (`allowTypeSyntax` / `resolveTypeSyntax`). `type` aliases are skipped as `Pass` in any scope, so they do not bind the name and a nested alias is not `type alias statement not at top level`. Annotation-only statements do not bind a name; a second annotation is not `'x' redeclared at top level` or `type annotation on 'x' may only appear at its first declaration` (including a later `def` with a parameter type, return type, or `[T]`). Annotations, return types, `cast` operands, and alias definitions are not resolved in the enclosing scope when `resolveTypeSyntax` is on, and they are not left unresolved when it is off. `def f[S, T]` and `type Foo[X] = …` fail to parse instead of being accepted with the type variables unbound. `isinstance(...)` is a normal call, not `isinstance() is not yet supported`. `cast(...)` on the left of `=` or `+=` is the generic non-lvalue error, not `cannot assign to 'cast(...)'`.

### `src/test/native/windows/file_test.cc`

Empty, relative, mixed-slash, `.` / `..`, and drive forms without a trailing `\` are false (`c`, `c:`, `c:/`, `\\?\c:/`, `c:\foo/bar`, `c:\foo\.`, `c:\foo\.\bar`, `c:\foo\..\bar`, with or without `\\?\`). All four UNC combinations (name and target each with and without a `\\?\` prefix) create junctions that report as links, and a file under the target is visible through every junction, including a file created after the junction. Dangling targets succeed. The same target again is success. A different target is `kAlreadyExistsWithDifferentTarget`. An existing empty directory, a non-empty directory, or a file at the junction name is `kAlreadyExistsButNotJunction`. An exclusive open of that name directory still returns that code. An exclusive open of the target directory still allows creation.

Success covers a file, an empty directory, a junction, a dangling junction whose target was removed, and a junction whose target directory is exclusively open. `kDoesNotExist` covers a missing path and a child whose parent is a file. A non-empty directory is `kDirectoryNotEmpty`. An exclusive open of a file, of a directory (`FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`), or of the junction itself (`FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT`, not followed) is `kAccessDenied`.

### `src/test/native/windows/util_test.cc`
- Bazel lines: 392
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - The test locks the Windows `AsExecutablePathForCreateProcess` contract. Zel has no short-path, quote, `MAX_PATH`, or `\\?\` fallback for an executable, and local spawns pass `argv0` straight to `std::process::Command`.
  - An empty path fails with "should not be empty" and leaves the extended path empty. A quoted path such as `"cmd.exe"` fails with "path should not be quoted".
  - A drive-less absolute path (`/dev/null`, `/usr/bin/bash`, `\bar.exe`) fails with "path is absolute". A path containing `..` (`foo\..\bar.exe`, or a long `c:\…\..\foo.exe`) fails with "path is not normalized" and does not take the extended-path fallback.
  - A separator-free name whose length is at least `MAX_PATH - 4` fails with "a file name but too long". That limit is `MAX_PATH - 4`, not `MAX_PATH`.
  - A relative path with separators (`foo\bar.exe`) is joined to the current directory and returned quoted. The error is empty, the result is longer than the input, and the relative path is the suffix except for the closing quote.
  - An absolute path of length `MAX_PATH - 5` is quoted unchanged. Shortening is not attempted, so a missing file of that length is still accepted, and the extended path stays empty.
  - An absolute path of length `MAX_PATH - 4` or more that does not exist fails with a `GetShortPathNameW` error and an empty extended path. If the file exists but its 8.3 form is still too long, the error contains "cannot shorten the path".
  - An existing long path whose 8.3 name fits is returned quoted as that short name. The test expects `"<root>\AAAAAA~1.BAT"` for a long run of `a`s plus `.bat`.
  - A missing absolute, normalized plain executable that cannot be shortened falls back: the quoted original path plus an extended path of `\\?\` plus the input. A `.bat` path is refused that fallback and surfaces the `GetShortPathNameW` error.

Update mode therefore does not restore deleted facts for a non-reproducible extension without a rerun, does not rerun a reproducible extension whose facts were edited, and does not rebuild the facts section from the hidden lockfile after `MODULE.bazel.lock` is deleted. Error mode does not fail with `has changed its facts` when a reproducible extension's facts were edited or when a re-evaluation returns different facts.

### `src/test/py/bazel/bzlmod/remote_repo_contents_cache_test.py`
- Bazel lines: 2813
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - `--experimental_remote_repo_contents_cache` is a startup flag that makes Bazel store reproducible repository-rule results in the remote action cache and, on a hit, inject the repo into an in-memory overlay file system instead of re-running the rule. Zel parses the flag and treats it as inert, so a reproducible repo is always fetched onto the local external directory.
  - With the local repo contents cache disabled (`--repo_contents_cache=`), a remote hit survives `clean --expunge` and leaves repo files absent on disk (`BUILD` does not exist) while still allowing the build to use them. Zel refetches and writes a real directory. `--noexperimental_remote_repo_contents_cache` forces that refetch in Bazel; in Zel the flag does not change fetch behavior.
  - A remote hit is keyed by a chain of action-cache entries: the predeclared-input hash, then recorded inputs (`rctx.watch`, declared `environ`, watched labels, including different values and different input sets such as `.sh` vs `.exe`). Restoring a previous value skips the rule even after expunge, and two workspaces sharing the remote cache reuse an entry when the recorded environment matches and miss when it does not. Zel does not upload or look up repository trees in the remote cache.
  - The local on-disk `--repo_contents_cache` is a different cache. This test uses it only to show that a local hit materializes a real tree and that, after that cache is discarded, the remote cache still hits and does not materialize the tree. Zel’s local cache never falls through to a remote repo-contents entry.
  - On a remote hit, only files Bazel or a local action actually reads are downloaded: another repo reading the tree fully materializes it (including empty directories); a local `no-cache` action materializes the source file, directory, or symlink it needs, including symlink chains and targets reached only by resolving links; a remote action can consume the input without materializing the repo. Reads through a source directory and per-file prefetch of an overlapping file in the same build must not conflict. Zel has no overlay, so every fetched file is already on disk.
  - `.bzl` and `REPO.bazel` files are prefetched onto the native filesystem during injection, including when the loaded path is a symlink whose target name is not itself a `.bzl`, and when that symlink points at another repo. Other files stay virtual. `bazel run` of a cached module extension repo (buildozer) runs without materializing `MODULE.bazel`. Zel always materializes the fetched tree.
  - Repos whose symlink chain escapes into the main repo are not uploaded (`CROSS_REPO_SYMLINKS_CACHEABLE` is false) and are refetched after expunge, with the absolute link left unreplanted. A symlink into another repo is stored and reproduced identically by full materialization and by lazy action-input materialization; a remote action can upload the native target through that symlink, and a local action needs the link on disk. A command with no remote cache must refetch a repo that the same server only holds in memory. Zel does not apply these cacheability or materialization rules.
  - If a CAS blob for a not-yet-materialized file disappears, Bazel reports a transient remote-cache error, retries (recovering `@my_repo`, then `@platforms`), refetches, and fully materializes the repo; a later expunge can hit again and prefetch only the file the new target needs. A cached fetch restarted after a memory-pressure Skyframe drop must not drop or truncate the native copies of prefetched `.bzl` and `REPO.bazel` files. Zel has neither failure path.
  - Reversing the dependency direction between two repos that keep the same predeclared hashes must not cycle in the cache lookup, and both repos hit after the new direction has been cached once. Zel does not have that remote lookup graph.
  - After a cached repo is materialized, a contents proxy marks the on-disk files unchanged, so evicting the remote entry does not cause a visible refetch, and switching from the overlay to disk does not invalidate Skyframe nodes for an unchanged target. Zel never injects that proxy or that overlay-to-disk transition.

Overlaying a directory on `/etc`, mounting `/etc` onto a path under `/tmp`, and keeping `/tmp/tree` the same inside and outside the sandbox do not happen.
  - `--sandbox_tmpfs_path` must be absolute and is stored, but no empty writable tmpfs is mounted. A path under `/tmp` still shows its host files, and `/etc` is not emptied.
  - There is no hermetic `/tmp`. A file an action creates under `/tmp` remains on the host and is visible to another action. Inputs, runfiles, external repos, and an output base that live under `/tmp` stay reachable only because nothing hides `/tmp`. `--package_path` is reported by `info` and is not used to load packages, so the extra package root in that case is not searched.

  - `--sandbox_debug` still drops `Use --sandbox_debug to see verbose messages from the sandbox and retain the sandbox build root for debugging` and keeps the sandbox directory. It does not print linux-sandbox’s `child exited normally with code 1`. `--experimental_use_hermetic_linux_sandbox` does not switch to a rootless sandbox that hardlinks inputs and mounts only `--sandbox_add_mount_pair` paths.
  - Tree-artifact outputs are pre-created, including an empty directory. A tree artifact in runfiles is one directory symlink, not an expanded tree of per-file symlinks. After `cd` into it, `file` is a regular file, so the sandboxed `sh_test` passes; Bazel expects it to fail with `'file' is not a regular file` because the expanded runfile is a symlink.

### `src/test/shell/bazel/bazel_symlink_test.sh`
- Bazel lines: 922
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-analysis/src/starlark_rule_actions.rs`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - `target_path` is not kept as the given string. Execution in `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-analysis/src/action.rs` and `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-exec/src/lib.rs` links to `<execroot>/<target_path>` (absolute paths stay absolute). `readlink` is that path, and a relative target is not resolved from the symlink’s directory, so a basename such as `file` points at `<execroot>/file` rather than the sibling output. If `symlink` itself fails, zel copies the target bytes or reports a missing input instead of leaving a dangling link.
  - Input digests follow symlinks (`path_digest` in `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-exec/src/lib.rs`). A dangling link hashes as `<missing>` for every target string, so a genrule that only depends on an unresolved symlink is not rerun when `link_target` changes, in memory or from the on-disk action cache. The symlink action itself is also never a cache hit, because its output digest is missing. Replacing a symlink with a real file, or the reverse, does change the digest.
  - Nothing checks that a `declare_symlink` output is a symlink, or that a declared file is not a dangling symlink. `actions.write` on a declared symlink writes a normal file. A spawn that leaves a dangling symlink as a normal output succeeds. Bazel fails those with `declared output '…' is not a symlink` and `declared output '…' is a dangling symbolic link`.
  - Sandbox inputs are symlinks to the execroot path (`/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-sandbox/src/sandbox.rs`), so a sandboxed `readlink` of a symlink input is that path, not the original target. Runfiles (`/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-exec/src/runfiles_tree.rs`) are absolute execroot links, not the relative `target_path`, so a runfile symlink can resolve outside the runfiles tree.
  - A cycle between two `symlink` actions is reported as `cycle in the action graph`, not `cycle in dependency graph`.
  - `--windows_enable_symlinks` is only defined. Symlink creation is Unix `symlink` and is unsupported on other platforms.

- Verdict: partial

Bazel schedules each run as its own action, so `--local_resources=cpu=3` with `--local_test_jobs=0`, and `--local_test_jobs=3` with extra CPU, cap how many of those runs overlap. The worker count also treats `--local_test_jobs=0` as `--jobs` rather than “no count limit, CPU only” (`/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-server/src/exec_phase.rs`).
  - `--experimental_cancel_concurrent_tests=on_failed` is not applied. With `--runs_per_test_detects_flakes`, every run still executes. There are no `CANCELLED:` lines, and the flaky summary counts all runs (`failed in 3 out of 5`) instead of the runs that finished before cancellation (`failed in 1 out of 3`).
  - A test that leaves `TEST_PREMATURE_EXIT_FILE` in place still passes. Bazel deletes that file after the spawn and, if it was present, fails the test and appends `-- Test exited prematurely (TEST_PREMATURE_EXIT_FILE exists) --`.
  - A rule `env` entry `TEST_NAME=foo` is passed through. Bazel refuses to run the test with `cannot set env variable TEST_NAME=foo because TEST_NAME is reserved`.

  - Coverage environment, including `CC_CODE_COVERAGE_SCRIPT`, is merged into the rule environment and applied after `--test_env`. Bazel applies that coverage map with put-if-absent after both `--test_env` and the rule `env`, so `GCOV` / `BAZEL_LLVM_COV` (as `COVERAGE_GCOV_PATH` and `LLVM_COV`) and `CC_CODE_COVERAGE_SCRIPT` lose to `--test_env`, and the rule `env` wins over both. Zel keeps the coverage values in all three cases.
  - Fallback `test.xml` is synthesized in-process instead of by `generate-xml.sh`. The suite and case name are only the target name (`success`, `test`, `x`), `duration` and `time` are always `0`, and shard names are not `dir/test_shard_1/2`. A timeout log is not rewritten with `?` for invalid bytes or with `generate-xml.sh`’s `]]>` split, so the fallback does not match `dir/success`, `dir/test_shard_2/2`, or `+local_repository+a/x`.
  - Undeclared-output `MANIFEST` and `ANNOTATIONS` are written under the attempt directory and deleted with it, so `bazel-testlogs/.../test.outputs_manifest/` stays empty. `test.outputs` from the last attempt is copied. Failed attempts are not published as `test_attempts/attempt_N.outputs` (zip or loose files).
  - `--run_under` is resolved only when the first word equals the configured target’s canonical label. `@run//:under` and `@run//:under.sh` do not match `@@…//:under`, so the literal label is executed. Bazel runs the external `sh_binary` or the exported `under.sh` and forwards options such as `-c`.
  - A passing attempt does not emit a `PASS` event, so `--experimental_ui_debug_all_events` never prints `PASS: //:flaky` or `PASS: //:pass`. Bazel does, including after a flaky retry.

### `src/test/shell/bazel/external_starlark_execute_test.sh`
- Bazel lines: 120
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-bzlmod/src/ctx.rs`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - A successful `repository_ctx.execute` must finish its descendants before it returns. Bazel runs the command under process-wrapper: the child calls `setsid`, and once that direct child has exited the wrapper SIGKILLs its process group and, on Linux with `PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER`, any children that left the group (`TerminateAndWaitForAll`). `test_children_waited` backgrounds `(sleep 30; echo bar > data.txt)` and then writes `baz`; the copied file must still contain `baz`. Zel `run_process` also calls `setsid`, then `try_wait`s only the direct pid and returns, so that background writer stays alive and can replace `baz` with `bar` after `execute` returns.
  - Killing the client during `ctx.execute` must kill that command and make the client exit non-zero. Bazel catches SIGTERM, cancels the server command, and `Command.execute` (`KILL_SUBPROCESS_ON_INTERRUPT`) `destroy()`s process-wrapper, which SIGKILLs the process group. `test_interrupted_children_waited` requires `waiter.sh` to be dead without reaching `echo finished`. Zel's client catches SIGTERM and sends `Cancel`, and a dropped Run stream marks the command cancelled, but `run_process` never reads that flag or `global_cancel_requested` (only action `process_wrapper::run` does). It SIGKILLs only the direct child, and only after the timeout (default 600s). The `setsid` session survives the client, so `waiter.sh` keeps running and overwrites `status` with `finished`.

### `src/test/shell/bazel/path_mapping_test.sh`
- Bazel lines: 1343
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - `--experimental_output_paths=strip` is accepted as `off` or `strip` and is never applied. Command lines, action keys, and disk and remote cache keys keep config-specific `bazel-out/<mnemonic>/...` paths, so fastbuild versus opt, dotted or hyphenated platform names, and input-preserving transitions do not share cache hits.
  - Opt-in does nothing. Starlark `supports-path-mapping`, `--modify_execution_info` for `CppCompile`, `CppModuleMap`, and `CppArchive`, and the hard-coded mnemonics that strip without that requirement are ignored. Java compile, header, and resource-jar actions always record `supports-path-mapping=1`, and nothing reads it.
  - A path-mapped spawn is not forced into a sandbox, remote execution, or a sandbox-capable worker. `Javac` with `--strategy=Javac=local` is not rejected with "requires sandboxing due to path mapping", and `local,sandboxed` does not prefer the sandbox. Multiplex workers are not held back until multiplex sandboxing is enabled.

### `src/test/shell/bazel/remote/uds_proxy.py`
- Bazel lines: 63
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - Bazel runs a standalone process that binds an `AF_UNIX` stream socket at `argv[0]`, listens with backlog 64, and accepts forever.
  - Each accepted connection is handed to a daemon thread that dials TCP `host:port` from `argv[1]` and copies both directions with `select` in 4096-byte reads.

Bazel reports that fetch error, including the traceback and `This is the failure message`, as the repository failure.

### `src/test/shell/bazel/testing_server.py`
- Bazel lines: 177
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - No port of this external-repository HTTP fixture. `/workspace/zel-cursor/scripts/bzlmod_harness/server.py` is a different server: it binds `127.0.0.1` to `hconf.PORT`, serves `VBZ/www`, and special-cases `/echo`, `/auth` (Basic `user:pass`, realm `x`, empty 401 body), `/redir` (302 to `/hello.txt`), `/loop`, `/err500`, and `/noname`. `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-bzlmod/src/download.rs` `serve` accepts a fixed number of connections and writes caller-supplied bytes. Neither implements the CLI or responses below.
  - Optional positional `mode` and `target`, plus `--unix_socket` and `--dump_headers`. `always` plus a target always serves that file. `redirect` plus a target sends 301 with `Location` set to the raw target. `404` sets not-found. `timeout` hangs. `auth` requires credentials and, when a target is present, also pins the file. Any other mode, or `always`/`redirect` without a target, serves files from the working directory. `--dump_headers` applies together with every mode.
  - Without `--unix_socket`, the process picks `random.randrange(32760, 59760)` and retries forever on `socket.error`. Darwin listens with `AF_INET6` on `('', port)`; every other platform uses `AF_INET` on `('', port)`. It writes `{port}\nstarted\n` to stdout, flushes, and closes stdout, then writes `Serving forever on {port}.\n` to stderr.
  - `--unix_socket` builds a `UnixStreamServer` on that path and writes only `Serving forever on {path}.\n` to stderr. There is no port or `started` line. On Windows the Unix server class is not imported, so that flag fails before the accept loop. `GET` with a missing `client_address` sets it to the string `localhost` before handling the request. `HEAD` does not.
  - `GET` order is header dump, then hang, then 404, then redirect, then auth or file. `404` is status 404 and an empty body. Redirect is status 301 and a `Location` header. `timeout` is `while True: time.sleep(1)` after the dump, with no status line. Responses use `HTTP/1.0`, `Content-type: text/html`, and no `Content-Length`; the body ends when the connection closes. Each request also gets the default access log on stderr.
  - A successful `GET` sends that 200 header block, then the raw file bytes. The path is the URL with one leading character removed, joined to the working directory, unless a pinned filename replaces it. `os.path.join` drops the working directory when the remainder is absolute. The file is opened only after the 200 is sent, so a missing file leaves the client with 200 and a dropped connection, and the traceback goes to stderr.
  - With auth, `Authorization` must be exactly `Basic Zm9vOmJhcg==` (`foo:bar`) or `Bearer TOKEN`. Anything else, including a missing header, is 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="Bazel"` and `Content-type: text/html`. Under Python 3 the body is `Bad authorization header: ` plus the `repr` of the header bytes (`b'...'`). A non-ASCII header raises `UnicodeEncodeError` before that response.
  - `--dump_headers` rewrites that file on every `GET` with `json.dumps` of the header dict. Names `Host` and `User-Agent` are dropped by exact match. Duplicate names keep the last value. Non-ASCII values are escaped with `\u`.
  - `HEAD` is always 200, `Content-type: text/html`, and an empty body. It ignores auth, 404, redirect, timeout, the pinned file, and header dump. When `serve_forever` returns, stderr gets `Goodbye.\n`.

Bazel schedules one `TestRunnerAction` per run. The helper fails when more than three files are present in the shared temp directory, so those ten runs never overlap and neither `--local_test_jobs=3 --local_resources=cpu=10` nor `--local_resources=cpu=3` (flag omitted) caps concurrent runs at 3.

Bazel’s scheduler width stays `--jobs` (3). With local test jobs enabled, each test requests only `localTestCount=1` (0 CPU, 0 MB), so `cpu=10` does not lower that cap.

### `src/test/shell/integration/bazel_worker_multiplexer_test.sh`
- Bazel lines: 632
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-sandbox/src/worker.rs`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - A changed worker binary or runfile keeps the same multiplex process. Spawns are built with empty `tool_inputs`, so the worker-files hash never changes, and `WorkerKey` treats that hash as pool identity. Bazel keeps the hash out of the pool key, rejects the live worker, logs `Work multiplex-worker (id N) can no longer be used, because its files have changed on disk` plus `path: <old hex> -> <new hex>`, and the next request runs in a new process whose counter is 1.
  - `--experimental_worker_multiplex_sandboxing` with `supports-multiplex-sandboxing` does not give each request its own sandbox. Bazel stages inputs under `__sandbox/<workerId>/<workspace>`, sets `WorkRequest.sandbox_dir` to that relative path, and moves outputs back. Zel uses one shared `worker-<id>-<mnemonic>/execroot/<workspace>` as the process cwd, symlinks inputs there, and leaves `sandbox_dir` empty, so `--ignore_sandbox` still sees the inputs. The suite expects `java.nio.file.NoSuchFileException`. Concurrent multiplex requests share that directory.
  - Junk on the multiplex stdout becomes `worker process terminated unexpectedly`. Bazel reports `Worker process returned an unparseable WorkResponse!`, the stdout-protocol explanation, and a recording-stream dump that contains `I'm a poisone`. A hard crash’s stderr is wrapped as `---8<---8<--- Start of log, file at <absolute path> ---8<---8<---` through `---8<---8<--- End of log ---8<---8<---`, truncated at 8192 bytes. Zel writes `Start of log, file at <mnemonic>` and `End of log` with no path and no truncation snippet. Parse failures and a closed stream are the same error, so `did not return a WorkResponse` and `returned an unparseable WorkResponse` are not distinguished.
  - `--worker_verbose` does not log `Created new <non-sandboxed|sandboxed> multiplex Work multiplex-worker (id N, key hash H), logging to <output_base>/(bazel|blaze)-workers/multiplex-worker-N-Work.log`, `Destroying Work multiplex-worker (id N, key hash H)`, or `Build completed, shutting down worker pool...`. Log files are `bazel-workers/worker-<id>-<mnemonic>.log`. The next build after `shutdown` does not delete `*.log` in that directory.
  - `bazel clean` leaves the pool running and does not log `Clean command is running, shutting down worker pool...` or the destroy line, so the same multiplex process is reused. `--worker_quit_after_build` does destroy the pool at the end of the build, so the work counter resets.

An unchanged rebuild logs `hit count=1` (`stable-status.txt`) and `miss count=1` (`volatile-status.txt`), and those counts are per command, not accumulated. Dropping the in-memory graph with `--nocheck_visibility` then logs `hit count=3` (`stable-status.txt`, `foo.out`, `bar.out`) and `miss count=1`. Setting the size to 100 drops every entry, so the next build logs `hit count=0` and `miss count=4`. `bazel info` does not change those stats, and the same size on the next build is a hit again. Size 0 disables the cache. The server log contains `CacheFileDigestsModule` with `Cache stats` when the cache is on and `Disabled cache` when it is 0. Zel parses the flag into `ExecOptions.cache_computed_file_digests` and never reads it. `COMPUTED_DIGEST_CACHE` stays unset, so every digest is read from disk, and none of those log lines or counts are produced.

On macOS, if the hard limit is unlimited or above `kern.maxfilesperproc`, the soft limit becomes `kern.maxfilesperproc`. On Windows the soft limit is left as it is. A genrule that runs `ulimit -S -n` therefore prints that raised value. Zel calls `setrlimit` only for `RLIMIT_CORE` under `--unlimit_coredumps`, so the genrule prints the process's original soft limit on every OS.

Exit 71 is returned as 71. `kill -ABRT` is returned as 134 (`128 + signal`). `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-sandbox/src/bin/zel-process-wrapper.rs` can echo, return an exit code, and re-raise the child's signal, and on spawn failure it prints `process-wrapper: execvp({}, ...): {e}` including `(os error N)`. It rejects `-W` and does not run in a mount or user namespace.

Process-wrapper does not install those handlers. A timeout there is always reported as `SIGALRM` (exit 142), including when the child exits during the delay.
  - `-T 3 -t 3` around `echo before; sleep 1000; echo after` fails after printing `before`. `-T 2 -t 30` with a `SIGTERM` trap that exits 17 yields 17 or 143. `-T 2 -t 3` with `SIGTERM` ignored yields 137 or 143. Zel's wrapper uses `-t` as the timeout and `-k` as the delay, and it does not return the child's code once the deadline has fired.

Successful `-M`/`-m` mounts log `bind mount: <source> -> <target>` (a repeated target is mounted again and the second source wins). A relative `-m` fails with `The -m option must be used with absolute paths only.` An `-m` that is not strictly after `-M`, including when another flag sits between them, fails with `The -m option must be strictly preceded by an -M option.` `LinuxSandboxCommandLineBuilder` only emits `-D`, `-M`, and `-m`. It does not open a debug file, close extra fds, or mount anything.
  - `-l` and `-L` capture `echo out` and `echo err >&2` as those two files. `-w /tmp` lets the child delete a file it created under `/tmp` when the host `/tmp` is writable. `-w` of the canonical `/dev/shm` does the same for `/dev/shm`. The builder can place `-l`, `-L`, and `-w` on an argv. Nothing in Zel applies those redirects or writable mounts for this helper.
  - `-S` writes an `ExecutionStatistics` protobuf. `spend_cpu_time` must land in the ranges user 10–19 / system 0–9, user 0–9 / system 10–19, and user 10–25 / system 10–25, with the sandbox killed only after `-T 100`. Zel has no `spend_cpu_time`. Process-wrapper stats come from `wait4` rusage and are not checked against those ranges.
  - With a real cgroup v1 memory controller, `-C` plus `memory.limit_in_bytes=1000000` lets `/bin/echo hi there` succeed, and `1000` fails with no `hi there`. Cgroup v2 does the same under `systemd-run --user --scope` using `memory.max`, after enabling the parent's `memory` controller. A mock directory with `memory.peak` or `memory.max_usage_in_bytes` set to `41943040` makes `-S` report `maxrss` `40960` (bytes / 1024). Zel never joins a cgroup or reads those files.

### `src/test/shell/integration/profiler_test.sh`
- Bazel lines: 96
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-server/src/observability.rs`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - `--profile` still writes Chrome counter events (`"ph":"C"`), but each args key is the lane title (`"CPU usage (Bazel)"`, `"CPU usage (total)"`, `"Memory usage (Bazel)"`, `"Memory usage (total)"`, `"System load average"`). Bazel uses `cpu`, `system cpu`, `memory`, `system memory`, and `load`, so every `expect_log` in this file fails.
  - `CPU usage (Bazel)` and `CPU usage (total)` are the same number: process user+system CPU seconds divided by wall time, clamped at 64. Bazel records process CPU delta/wall as `cpu`, and system CPU load times the processor count as `system cpu` (that value may be negative).
  - Both memory lanes are peak RSS in MiB (`ru_maxrss`). Bazel records JVM heap plus non-heap used MiB as `memory`, and system used memory as `system memory` (on Linux, `(MemTotal − MemFree) / 1024`).
  - Those counters are two identical samples at t=0 and t=wall, in one bucket the length of the command. Bazel samples every 200 ms on a background thread into 1-second buckets for the whole invocation. Events also omit Bazel’s `cname` (`good`, `olive`, `rail_load`, `bad`, `generic_work`).
  - `--experimental_collect_load_average_in_profiler` is never read. The 1-minute load is always emitted, including 0, which the shared near-zero skip then drops from `args`. Bazel records it only when the flag is on and the sample is greater than 0, under the key `load`.
  - `--experimental_collect_skyframe_counts_in_profiler` is never read. There are no `SkyFunction (ACTION_EXECUTION|CONFIGURED_TARGET|PACKAGE)` counters with adjacent `(total)` and `(done)` series. Bazel walks the Skyframe graph each sample and also records `BZL_LOAD`, `GLOB`, `GLOBS`, and `ASPECT`.
  - Network and worker lanes are always present as 0 under the lane name (`Network Up/Down usage (total)`, `Total worker memory usage`), so `args` stay empty. With the flags at their default of true, Bazel records `system network up/down (Mbps)` and `workers memory`, plus per-mnemonic worker memory on Linux and macOS. PSI and resource-estimation lanes stay absent even when those flags are turned on.

It deletes each sandbox directory when the action finishes, and deletes the runner directory at the end of the command.

### `src/test/shell/integration/spend_cpu_time.cc`
- Bazel lines: 166
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - No program burns a requested amount of this process’s user and system CPU time. `zel-sandbox` only reads `getrusage` after a wrapped child (`process_wrapper.rs` `user_time` / `system_time`). `zel-test-worker` sleeps on a wall clock (`--sleep_ms`).
  - `argc != 3` prints `Usage: <argv[0] or spend_cpu_time> <user_time_seconds> <system_time_seconds>` to stderr and exits 1. Anything else is accepted: `atoi` on each argument, with no range or numeric check. A value `<= 0` skips that phase.
  - System time is burned first, then user time. Each phase loops until `RUSAGE_SELF` `ru_stime` or `ru_utime`, truncated to milliseconds (`sec * 1000 + usec / 1000`), reaches `seconds * 1000`. `SubtractOrZero` treats an already-larger reading as done. There is no second system-time top-up after the user phase, so user-time spinning can push system time past the request, and system-time spinning can already satisfy the user-time request.
  - System-time spinning calls `getcwd` into a `MAXPATHLEN` buffer, then `chdir`s to that path until wall time from `gettimeofday` covers the remaining milliseconds. `getcwd` or `chdir` failure calls `err(EXIT_FAILURE, …)` (libc message on stderr, exit 1) and does not print the summary.
  - User-time spinning is a `volatile uint64_t` count to `1000000`, repeated while `clock()` CPU time, in milliseconds (`1000 * delta / CLOCKS_PER_SEC`), is still short. `clock()` failure is ignored. The inner stop uses process CPU time. The outer stop uses user time only.
  - On success it prints `Total user time wasted: <ms> ms` and `Total system time wasted: <ms> ms` from a fresh `getrusage` and exits 0. `getrusage` failure is the same `err(EXIT_FAILURE, …)` path.

A `config_setting` that does not match fails with `target configuration didn't match config_setting <label>`. `select()` on the attribute expresses OR, inverse, and composed constraints. Aliases to constraint values and to incompatible targets follow the real target, and `target_compatible_with` on an `alias` itself makes dependents incompatible. `filegroup`, `cc_import`, and Starlark rules participate the same way.

Building that flag fails as incompatible; under `:all` the flag and the referenced target are skipped while an unrelated target in the package is built. Examples: `c:\foo\bar1` from `c:\foo\bar2` is `..\bar1`; `c:\foo\bar` from `c:\` is `foo\bar`; identical paths are empty; `c:\` from `c:\a\b\c` is `..\..\..\`; `foo\bar1` from `fo` is `..\foo\bar1`; empty from `foo\bar` is `..\..\`; `foo\bar` from empty is `foo\bar`. ### `third_party/ijar/classfile.cc`
- Bazel lines: 2030
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - `StripClass` rewrites a JVM class file into an interface class. Zel has no class-file parser or stripper. Header jars are a Turbine or JavacTurbine spawn from `java_create_header_action` in `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-analysis/src/java_native.rs`. The vendored ijar tree under `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-bazel-tools/resources/third_party/ijar` has zip I/O only. Its `BUILD` still lists `classfile.cc`, and that source is absent.
  - The magic must be `0xCAFEBABE`, or the process aborts. An unknown constant-pool tag copies the input bytes and still returns keep. A class-level annotation of type `Lkotlin/Metadata;` also copies the bytes unchanged.
  - A class that has an `EnclosingMethod` attribute returns keep false and writes nothing, so the caller omits that entry. Every other class is rewritten. Private fields, `<clinit>`, private methods, and package-private synthetic methods that are not bridges are omitted. Surviving members lose `Code`, `StackMapTable`, `LineNumberTable`, `LocalVariableTable`, `LocalVariableTypeTable`, `SourceFile`, `Synthetic`, `BootstrapMethods`, and `SourceDebugExtension`.
  - Kept attributes are `Exceptions`, `Signature`, `Deprecated`, `EnclosingMethod`, `InnerClasses`, `AnnotationDefault`, `ConstantValue`, runtime-visible and runtime-invisible annotations, parameter annotations, and type annotations, `MethodParameters`, `NestHost`, `NestMembers`, `Record`, `PermittedSubclasses`, and the opaque blobs `Scala`, `ScalaSig`, `ScalaInlineInfo`, `TASTY`, and `TurbineTransitiveJar`. `InnerClasses` is written last. A non-anonymous entry stays when the inner class is already referenced, its name was taken from a descriptor or signature, or its outer class is this class, and that pull then keeps the outer class and the inner name. `NestMembers` keeps a class only when it is already referenced or named in those signatures. The output constant pool is the reachable subset, and `long` and `double` still occupy two slots.
  - Any other attribute is skipped. `com.android.tools.r8.SynthesizedClass` and `SynthesizedClassV2` are silent. Each other unknown name is printed once on stderr. A bad constant-pool index, a type-annotation target outside `0x00`, `0x01`, and `0x10`–`0x17`, or an illegal annotation element tag aborts. A signature byte that `Expect` rejects calls `exit(1)`.
