### `third_party/ijar/zip.cc`
- Bazel lines: 1163
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-bzlmod/src/archive.rs`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - Zel has no zip writer. ijar writes entries with extract version 10, general-purpose flags 0, DOS time `30<<25 | 1<<21 | 1<<16` (2010-01-01 00:00:00), external attributes preserved, and extra length 0. It deflates only when the result is smaller than the stored payload, back-patches CRC and sizes, and emits a ZIP64 end record plus locator only when the entry count exceeds 65535 or the central-directory size or offset exceeds `0xFFFFFFFF`. Output is capped at 4GB. `Finish` is idempotent.
  - ijar rejects multi-disk archives when either classic disk number is non-zero, the per-disk entry count differs from the total, or the ZIP64 locator’s disk is non-zero or its total disk count is greater than 1. Zel never reads those fields and still extracts the archive.
  - ijar finds a ZIP64 end record at `eocd - 76` before using the locator, so a prepended preamble still resolves, and it keeps a ZIP64 field only when it matches the classic value or that value is the 16/32-bit sentinel. Zel consults only the absolute locator offset, and only when the classic entry count is `0xFFFF` or the classic directory offset is `0xFFFFFFFF`.
  - ijar places local headers at `physical_central_directory - recorded_offset + local_header_offset`. Zel uses the recorded local-header offset as a file offset. For a non-ZIP64 archive it reads the central directory at `eocd - cd_size` only when the low 32 bits of that sum equal the recorded offset.
  - ijar ignores the end-of-central-directory entry count and stops the directory walk on a central-directory signature, a digital signature, a ZIP64 end record, or a classic end record. Zel stops after the recorded count, or after `cd_size` bytes on the adjusted-start path, and any other signature is `Malformed Central Directory File Header; does not start with 02014b50`.
  - ijar copies entry names as raw bytes, truncated to `PATH_MAX - 1` and cut at the first NUL. Zel decodes every name with lossy UTF-8 and does not read the UTF-8 flag.
  - ijar rejects a local general-purpose bit other than bits 1, 2, 3, and 11, and a compression method other than store or deflate. Zel ignores those flags, inflates method 9 as deflate64, and for every other method copies `uncompressed_size` bytes.
  - ijar requires a non-zero, non-`0xFFFFFFFF` local size to match the central directory, and a stored entry to have equal compressed and uncompressed sizes. It then copies or inflates `compressed_size` bytes and does not check the CRC. Zel ignores the local sizes and CRC, and inflates until `uncompressed_size` bytes, truncating output that would exceed that limit.
  - ijar walks extra subfields with no remaining-length check, so a short ZIP64 payload consumes the following bytes. Zel stops when fewer than 4 bytes remain and returns `Truncated zip file` when a ZIP64 integer extends past the extra slice.
  - ijar passes each accepted entry’s name, external attributes, and bytes to a processor callback. Zel materializes files, directories, and symlinks, forces directory mode `0o755`, defaults other modes to `0o644`, and rejects a symlink target longer than 4096 bytes.

### `third_party/ijar/zip.h`
- Bazel lines: 169
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - `zipattr_is_dir` is true only when DOS external-attribute bit `0x10` is set. It ignores the Unix mode and a trailing slash. Zel has no ijar attribute helper. `parse_zip` in `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-bzlmod/src/archive.rs` treats a name ending in `/` as a directory with mode `0755`. Otherwise a Unix-made entry (version-made-by high byte 3) with a nonzero mode is a directory only if the high 16 bits include `S_IFDIR` (`0o040000`), and a symlink if they include `S_IFLNK`. The DOS `0x10` bit is used only in the remaining case, which also forces mode `0644`.

Zel keeps the unmasked high 16 bits for those Unix entries, substitutes `0755` or `0644` in the other cases, and on extract applies `(mode & 0o777) | 0o400` to files. Directories are created with `create_dir_all` and are not chmod'd from the zip attribute.
  - `ZipBuilder::NewFile` returns a builder-owned buffer. `FinishFile` defaults both deflate and CRC32 off. `WriteEmptyFile` is `NewFile(name, 0)` then `FinishFile(0)`. `Finish` runs at most once, the destructor calls it if it was skipped, and it writes the central directory, so `GetSize` is short until then. `Create` returns null and leaves `errno` set, and the output is capped at `estimated_size`. `EstimateSize` returns 0 on error. Zel does not build zips this way. Interface jars are produced by spawning the toolchain `single_jar`.

Zel reads the whole file with Java `ZipReader` end-of-central-directory rules and extracts to a directory. It has no accept/skip processor, no rewind, and no uncompressed output-size estimate.

### `third_party/java/proguard/proguard6.2.2/src/proguard/classfile/attribute/visitor/StackSizeComputer.java`
- Bazel lines: 389
- Zel counterpart: `none`
- Verdict: missing
- Differences:
  - Zel does not compute per-offset operand-stack sizes for a ProGuard code attribute. Non-code attributes are ignored. A code attribute resets reachability and the before/after sizes for `u4codeLength`, starts at stack 0, walks from offset 0, then visits each exception handler with the stack forced to 1.
  - An offset is reachable only after it is evaluated. The size before or after an unreachable offset throws `IllegalArgumentException` (`Unknown stack size before/after unreachable instruction offset [...]`). The maximum is the high-water mark of the incoming stack at each block and the stack after each instruction, including a handler entry of 1.
  - Each instruction subtracts `stackPopCount` and then adds `stackPushCount`. A negative size throws `IllegalArgumentException` naming the instruction, class, and method name plus descriptor. A block that starts at an already evaluated offset does not run again and does not check that the incoming size matches the stored size. The caller's stack is restored when the block returns.
  - The block ends on `ireturn`, `lreturn`, `freturn`, `dreturn`, `areturn`, `return`, `athrow`, `ret`, `goto`, `goto_w`, `jsr`, and `jsr_w`, and on every switch after each jump offset and the default have been walked. Constant-pool instructions never end the block. Other simple and variable instructions, and conditional branches after their target is walked, fall through.
  - `jsr` and `jsr_w` walk the target at the post-instruction size, then subtract 1 (the return address is popped) and walk the following instruction at that reduced size.
  - A `RuntimeException` from that walk is printed to stderr with the class name, method name plus descriptor, and the exception class and message, then rethrown. Tracing is off, so the method is not dumped.

  - Constants print bracketed values for int, long, float, double, string, UTF-8, module, package, class, method type, and name-and-type. Primitive arrays print type and length only. Dynamic and invoke-dynamic print the bootstrap index and then the name-and-type. Method handles print the reference kind and then the reference. Field, interface-method, and method refs print `class.name type`.
  - Program fields and methods print hex access flags and the external full description. Member attributes are printed only when the count is greater than 0, under `Class member attributes`. Program methods concatenate the name and descriptor with no space. Library methods insert a space, and library members do not walk attributes.
  - Attributes printed include unknown (by name), bootstrap methods, source file and dir, inner classes, enclosing method (name-and-type only if the index is non-zero), nest host and members, the full module attribute (flags, optional version, requires, exports, opens, uses, provides), module main class and packages, deprecated, synthetic, signature, constant value, method parameters, exceptions, and code (length, max locals, max stack, then instructions, exception table, and nested attributes). Stack-map and stack-map-table headers use the code attribute’s visitor marker, not the map attribute’s. Also line numbers, local variables, local-variable types, runtime-visible and invisible annotations, parameter annotations, and type annotations (those headers have no trailing colon), plus annotation defaults.
  - Ordinary instructions print `toString(offset)`. Constant instructions also print the referenced constant. `tableswitch` and `lookupswitch` add each case as `value: offset = jump, target = offset+jump` and a default line. Exception entries print `start -> end: handler` and the catch type only when `u2catchType != 0`.
  - Stack-map frames print same-zero as `Var: ..., Stack: (empty)`, same-one with the stack item on the same line, less-zero as `Var: -N`, more-zero with extra variables then `, Stack: (empty)`, and full frames as variables then `, Stack:` then stack items. Verification types are inline tokens: `[i]`, `[f]`, `[l]`, `[d]`, `[T]`, `[a:classname]`, `[n]`, `[u:offset]`, `[u:this]`.
  - Line numbers append `[source]` only when a source is set. Parameters print flags and a name, or empty brackets when the name index is 0. Local variables and local-variable types print `start -> start+length` with descriptor or signature and name. Requires always prints the version constant, including index 0. Exports, opens, and provides print their target or implementation constants.
  - Annotations print the type and element values. Parameter annotations include the parameter index. Type annotations print target info, the type-path count and steps (`kind`, argument index), then element values. Targets distinguish type parameter, super versus interface index, bound, empty, formal parameter, throws, local-variable ranges, catch, offset, and type argument. Element values cover constants (name `(default)` when the name index is 0, plus tag and constant), enum type and constant names, class names, nested annotations, and arrays. Inner-class entries always print inner, outer, and inner-name constants with no zero-index skip.

### `third_party/java/proguard/proguard6.2.2/src/proguard/optimize/TailRecursionSimplifier.java`

- Zel counterpart: `none`

- Differences:

  - The call is rewritten only when the next instruction is `ireturn`, `lreturn`, `freturn`, `dreturn`, `areturn`, or `return`, the call offset is outside every exception range, and the stack is empty after that return.

### `third_party/java/proguard/proguard6.2.2/src/proguard/optimize/gson/GsonDomainClassFinder.java`

Each failure, when a note printer is set, prints the reason and ` You should consider keeping this class and its fields.`, and the reason is passed through `externalClassName` on the internal name concatenated with the sentence, so `/` becomes `.`. A non-interface that passes is added to the domain pool, then non-synthetic fields are followed through their descriptors and signature attributes with the same visitor, and superclasses and subclasses are visited the same way. Interfaces are left out of the pool and their fields are not followed. Library classes are ignored. A class already in the pool is skipped entirely.

The 9.3.2 decompressors have no such check. `type` or a URL suffix of `tar.br` or `br` extracts. Bazel's format list ends at `7z`, and the error ends with `.deb or .7z`. `SUPPORTED_ARCHIVE_FORMATS` in this file is documentation and already matches that 9.3.2 list. A GNU sparse tar member (typeflag `S`) is skipped. USTAR and GNU entry names go through `from_utf8_lossy`, so a non-UTF-8 byte becomes U+FFFD. Bazel decodes those names as ISO-8859-1.
  - `http_file` writes `file/BUILD` with `repr(downloaded_file_path)`, which is Rust `Debug` (`\u{fc}` for a non-ASCII character). Bazel's printer leaves that character in the string (`\xHH` only for code points below 32). The generated `file/BUILD` then does not parse. ASCII paths match.
  - On Windows, `str(ctx.path(...))` uses the OS path (`\` separators). Bazel uses `/` and an uppercased drive, so the `downloaded_file_path` prefix check can reject a path Bazel accepts. `files` calls `ctx.symlink`, which errors off Unix. Bazel copies the file or creates a junction.

### `tools/test/CoverageOutputGenerator/java/com/google/devtools/coverageoutputgenerator/BranchCoverage.java`
- Bazel lines: 364
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-exec/resources/lcov_merger.sh`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - Evaluated state is a per-line sticky OR (`BitSet` by line number). Any evaluated branch on a line marks every branch on that line evaluated, and a later `evaluated=false` does not clear it. On merge or reprint, an unevaluated sibling is therefore reported as taken `0`, not `-`. The merger stores evaluated per `(line, block, branch)` and leaves that sibling as `-`.
  - Execution counts are `long` and wrap on overflow. The merger sums awk numbers (doubles), so totals past 2^53 are not exact and do not wrap at 2^64.
  - A negative line number throws `IndexOutOfBoundsException` from `BitSet` on set or get. The map also throws `IllegalStateException` once capacity reaches `0x40000000` (or when linear probing wraps a full table). The merger accepts those records and has no table-size cap.
  - A `null` branch id throws `IllegalArgumentException`, and a `null` block id throws on `equals` during lookup. The merger has no equivalent check.

### `tools/test/CoverageOutputGenerator/java/com/google/devtools/coverageoutputgenerator/BranchCoverageItem.java`
- Bazel lines: 90
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-exec/resources/lcov_merger.sh`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - `wasExecuted()` treats an empty `blockNumber` as a BA taken-code (`true` only when `nrOfExecutions == 2`) and any other block as executed when `nrOfExecutions > 0`. The merger has no such predicate: `BRH` counts a branch when taken is not `-` and is `> 0`, so taken `1` with an empty block id is a hit and taken `2` is not a distinct BA state.
  - The BA shape this type documents (empty block and branch ids, `nrOfExecutions` holding 0, 1, or 2) is not represented. `BA:` lines are ignored, and `--legacy_branches` / `--nolegacy_branches` are accepted and discarded, so every kept branch is stored and printed as `BRDA`.
  - `evaluated` is an independent boolean (not evaluated prints `-` even if a count is stored). The merger collapses that to one taken token: `-` means not evaluated and does not add, and any other token is accumulated with awk numeric conversion rather than a Java `long`.

### `tools/test/CoverageOutputGenerator/java/com/google/devtools/coverageoutputgenerator/BranchCoverageKey.java`
- Bazel lines: 99

- Differences:
  - Identity and print order are one `LC_ALL=C` byte string `sprintf("%012d", line) "," block "," branch`, not Java's int line compare followed by UTF-16 `String.compareTo` on block, then branch.
  - That encoding is not injective: `block="a,b", branch="c"` and `block="a", branch="b,c"` are one key and one summed `BRDA` line. Java `equals` and `compareTo` treat them as different keys.
  - Line order matches `int` order only for non-negative values that fit in 12 digits. Equal-width negatives sort by digit magnitude (`-1` before `-2`), and a 13-digit line sorts by its first digit (`1000000000000` before `999999999999`).
  - A block or branch byte below `','` (0x2C), or a non-ASCII id (UTF-8 bytes versus UTF-16 code units), sorts differently from `String.compareTo`.

Zel accepts four or more fields, tracks evaluated-ness per branch, treats any non-`-` value as evaluated (non-numeric becomes 0), and leaves a `-` branch unevaluated when another branch on the same line was taken.

### `tools/test/test-setup.sh`
- Bazel lines: 377
- Zel counterpart: `/workspace/zel-cursor/crates/zel-exec/resources/test-setup.sh`
- Verdict: partial
- Differences:
  - An unset or empty `HOME` is left unset. A relative `HOME` is prefixed with `$PWD`. Bazel replaces either case with `TEST_TMPDIR` and exports `HOME`.
  - The test and the coverage command are backgrounded directly, so the waited pid and process-group leader are the test itself. Bazel wraps them in a subshell, so that pid and group leader are the subshell and the test's parent is the subshell.
  - After `SIGTERM` (the timeout signal), Zel waits up to 15 seconds for the process group to exit before `SIGKILL`. Bazel `SIGKILL`s the group as soon as the waited child has exited.
  - Undeclared-output manifest sizes follow symlinks (`stat -L`). Bazel `stat` does not, so a symlink entry records the link size.
  - Manifest rows are written with `paste`, so `%` and backslashes stay literal. Bazel passes the path, size, and mime type through `printf` as the format string.
  - The output-directory prefix is stripped as a literal string, and leading or trailing whitespace in a path is kept. Bazel uses shell pattern removal and `read`, so glob characters in the directory can remain in the name and surrounding whitespace is stripped.
  - Sizes come from one batched `stat`. On BSD/macOS the `%N` name can be escaped, so the lookup misses and the size becomes `Could not stat <path>`. If the batch fails, every row gets that failure text. Bazel stats each file on its own.
